p0.original: In that rude state of society which precedes the extension of commerce and the improvement of manufactures; when those expensive luxuries, which commerce and manufactures can alone introduce, are altogether unknown; the person who possesses a large revenue, I have endeavoured to show in the third book of this Inquiry, can spend or enjoy that revenue in no other way than by maintaining nearly as many people as it can maintain. A large revenue may at all times be said to consist in the command of a large quantity of the necessaries of life. In that rude state of things, it is commonly paid in a large quantity of those necessaries, in the materials of plain food and coarse clothing, in corn and cattle, in wool and raw hides. When neither commerce nor manufactures furnish any thing for which the owner can exchange the greater part of those materials which are over and above his own consumption, he can do nothing with the surplus, but feed and clothe nearly as many people as it will feed and clothe. A hospitality in which there is no luxury, and a liberality in which there is no ostentation, occasion, in this situation of things, the principal expenses of the rich and the great. But these I have likewise endeavoured to show, in the same book, are expenses by which people are not very apt to ruin themselves. There is not, perhaps, any selfish pleasure so frivolous, of which the pursuit has not sometimes ruined even sensible men. A passion for cock-fighting has ruined many. But the instances, I believe, are not very numerous, of people who have been ruined by a hospitality or liberality of this kind; though the hospitality of luxury, and the liberality of ostentation have ruined many. Among our feudal ancestors, the long time during which estates used to continue in the same family, sufficiently demonstrates the general disposition of people to live within their income. Though the rustic hospitality, constantly exercised by the great landholders, may not, to us in the present times, seem consistent with that order which we are apt to consider as inseparably connected with good economy; yet we must certainly allow them to have been at least so far frugal, as not commonly to have spent their whole income. A part of their wool and raw hides, they had generally an opportunity of selling for money. Some part of this money, perhaps, they spent in purchasing the few objects of vanity and luxury, with which the circumstances of the times could furnish them; but some part of it they seem commonly to have hoarded. They could not well, indeed, do any thing else but hoard whatever money they saved. To trade, was disgraceful to a gentleman; and to lend money at interest, which at that time was considered as usury, and prohibited bylaw, would have been still more so. In those times of violence and disorder, besides, it was convenient to have a hoard of money at hand, that in case they should be driven from their own home, they might have something of known value to carry with them to some place of safety. The same violence which made it convenient to hoard, made it equally convenient to conceal the hoard. The frequency of treasure-trove, or of treasure found, of which no owner was known, sufficiently demonstrates the frequency, in those times, both of hoarding and of concealing the hoard. Treasure-trove was then considered as an important branch of the revenue of the sovereign. All the treasure-trove of the kingdom would scarce, perhaps, in the present times, make an important branch of the revenue of a private gentleman of a good estate.
p0.zh: 在商业扩展和制成品改进之前的这种粗鲁的社会状况中;当商业和制成品能够单独引进的昂贵奢侈品完全无人知晓时;拥有大量收入的人,我在本调查第三本书中努力表明,除了维持能够维持的几乎尽可能多的人之外,我无法花费或享受这些收入。可以说,在任何时候都有大量收入是生活必需品的指挥。 在这种无礼的状态下,通常用大量这些必需品、普通食品和粗俗衣服的材料、玉米和牛、羊毛和生皮来支付。 当商业和制成品都无法提供任何物物,使业主能够交换超出自己消费范围的大部分材料时,他无法用剩余物物物来做任何事情,只能用它来喂养和布衣几乎是用它来喂养和布衣的人。一种不奢侈的款待,一种不奢侈的自由主义,在这种事物的形势下,是富人和大人的主要开支. 但我同样努力在同一本书中 表明这些开支 人们不太愿意毁掉自己 也许没有,任何自私的乐趣 如此无意义, 追逐有时没有摧毁 甚至理智的人。爱打鸡巴已经毁了很多人。 但是,我认为,这些例子并不多,因为人们受到这种款待或自由的破坏;尽管奢侈的款待和自由的诱惑已经使许多人受到破坏。 在我们的封建祖先中,在同一个家庭里,庄园过去很长一段时间的存续,充分显示了人们在收入范围内生活的一般意愿. 虽然在当今时代,伟大的土地拥有者们不断采取的不成熟的好客态度,似乎与我们所认为的与良好的经济密不可分的秩序不相符合;但我们当然必须允许他们至少迄今保持节俭,因为通常情况下,他们并没有花光全部收入。 他们的羊毛和原始皮的一部分,一般都有为钱卖钱的机会。这笔钱的有些部分,也许,他们花在购买少数的虚荣和奢侈物品上,而时代的情况可以提供这些物品;但其中的有些部分似乎一般都囤积起来. 他们确实不能很好地做任何其他事情,只能囤积他们节省的金钱。贸易,对君子是无耻的;借利息,当时被认为是高利贷,禁止的,本来会更加如此. 在那些暴力和混乱的时代,此外,拥有囤积钱财是方便的,如果这些钱财被赶出自己的家门,他们可能有一些已知的价值的东西可以携带到某个安全的地方。同样的暴力使得囤积变得方便,也使得隐藏囤积变得同样方便.淘宝的频率,或发现的财宝的频率,没有已知的主人,充分证明了在那些时候,无论是囤积还是隐藏囤积的频率.宝藏后来被认为是君主收入的重要分支.王国的所有宝藏都很少,也许在当今的时代,会成为好庄园的私人绅士收入的重要分支.

p1.original: The same disposition, to save and to hoard, prevailed in the sovereign, as well as in the subjects. Among nations, to whom commerce and manufacture are little known, the sovereign, it has already been observed in the Fourth book, is in a situation which naturally disposes him to the parsimony requisite for accumulation. In that situation, the expense, even of a sovereign, cannot be directed by that vanity which delights in the gaudy finery of a court. The ignorance of the times affords but few of the trinkets in which that finery consists. Standing armies are not then necessary; so that the expense, even of a sovereign, like that of any other great lord can be employed in scarce any thing but bounty to his tenants, and hospitality to his retainers. But bounty and hospitality very seldom lead to extravagance; though vanity almost always does. All the ancient sovereigns of Europe, accordingly, it has already been observed, had treasures. Every Tartar chief, in the present times, is said to have one.
p1.zh: 在君主和臣民中,同样的处置方式,即拯救和囤积,都占上风。 在商业和制造业鲜为人知的各国中,主权者在第四本书中已经指出,这种局面自然使他陷入积累所需的公平条件。 在这种情况下,即使是君主的费用也不能由在法院的优雅中取悦的虚荣来支配。时代的无知只能承受微薄的磨损常备军队是没有必要的;这样,即使是君主的开支,就像任何其他大领主的开支,也只能用来为他的租户提供赏金,为他的留用者提供招待。 但是,赏金和款待很少导致奢侈;尽管虚荣几乎总是如此。 欧洲所有古代的君主, 因此,它已经被观察到, 有宝藏。 据说,在当今时代,每个鞑靼族酋长都有一位。

p2.original: In a commercial country, abounding with every sort of expensive luxury, the sovereign, in the same manner as almost all the great proprietors in his dominions, naturally spends a great part of his revenue in purchasing those luxuries. His own and the neighbouring countries supply him abundantly with all the costly trinkets which compose the splendid, but insignificant, pageantry of a court. For the sake of an inferior pageantry of the same kind, his nobles dismiss their retainers, make their tenants independent, and become gradually themselves as insignificant as the greater part of the wealthy burghers in his dominions. The same frivolous passions, which influence their conduct, influence his. How can it be supposed that he should be the only rich man in his dominions who is insensible to pleasures of this kind? If he does not, what he is very likely to do, spend upon those pleasures so great a part of his revenue as to debilitate very much the defensive power of the state, it cannot well be expected that he should not spend upon them all that part of it which is over and above what is necessary for supporting that defensive power. His ordinary expense becomes equal to his ordinary revenue, and it is well if it does not frequently exceed it. The amassing of treasure can no longer be expected; and when extraordinary exigencies require extraordinary expenses, he must necessarily call upon his subjects for an extraordinary aid. The present and the late king of Prussia are the only great princes of Europe, who, since the death of Henry IV. of France, in 1610, are supposed to have amassed any considerable treasure. The parsimony which leads to accumulation has become almost as rare in republican as in monarchical governments. The Italian republics, the United Provinces of the Netherlands, are all in debt. The canton of Berne is the single republic in Europe which has amassed any considerable treasure. The other Swiss republics have not. The taste for some sort of pageantry, for splendid buildings, at least, and other public ornaments, frequently prevails as much in the apparently sober senate-house of a little republic, as in the dissipated court of the greatest king.
p2.zh: 在一个商业国家, 拥有各种昂贵奢侈品的君主, 以与他统治的几乎所有大业主一样的方式, 自然地将他收入的很大一部分 用于购买这些奢侈品。 他的自己和邻国向他提供了大量费用高昂的金币,这些金币构成一个法庭精彩但微不足道的选美。 为了同类的卑劣的选美,他的贵族们解雇了他们的保留者,使他们的租户独立,逐渐变得像他领地中较富裕的堡垒中的大部分一样微不足道.同样的轻率的激情 影响着他们的行为 也影响着他何以推之,其国中独有富贵之人,不能感此等之乐乎? 如果他不这样做,他很可能这样做,就把大部分收入花在这些乐趣上,以致于削弱国家的防御能力,那么不能指望他不应该把支持这种防御能力所必需的全部部分花在他们身上。 他的普通开支变得与普通收入相等,如果不经常超过,那也很好.无法再预料到宝藏的积累;当非常紧急需要特别开支时,他必须要求他的臣民提供特别援助。普鲁士的现在和后来的国王是欧洲唯一的大王子,自从1610年法国的亨利四世去世后,他们应该已经积累了任何可观的财富.导致积累的教义在共和制和君主制政府中几乎一样少见. 意大利各共和国,荷兰联合省,都负债累累.伯尔尼州是欧洲单一的共和国,它积累了任何可观的财富. 其他瑞士共和国没有。 对某种美景的品味,对优美的建筑,至少,以及其他公共装饰品的品味,经常在显然清醒的参议院小共和国院中盛行,就像在最伟大的国王的消失的宫廷里一样。

p3.original: The want of parsimony, in time of peace, imposes the necessity of contracting debt in time of war. When war comes, there is no money in the treasury, but what is necessary for carrying on the ordinary expense of the peace establishment. In war, an establishment of three or four times that expense becomes necessary for the defence of the state; and consequently, a revenue three or four times greater than the peace revenue. Supposing that the sovereign should have, what he scarce ever has, the immediate means of augmenting his revenue in proportion to the augmentation of his expense; yet still the produce of the taxes, from which this increase of revenue must be drawn, will not begin to come into the treasury, till perhaps ten or twelve months after they are imposed. But the moment in which war begins, or rather the moment in which it appears likely to begin, the army must be augmented, the fleet must be fitted out, the garrisoned towns must be put into a posture of defence; that army, that fleet, those garrisoned towns, must be furnished with arms, ammunition, and provisions. An immediate and great expense must be incurred in that moment of immediate danger, which will not wait for the gradual and slow returns of the new taxes. In this exigency, government can have no other resource but in borrowing.
p3.zh: 在和平时期,缺乏公正,就必然需要在战争时期签订债务契约。 当战争到来时,国库里没有钱,而是需要什么来承担和平建立的一般费用. 在战争中,设立三四倍的费用成为保卫国家所必需的;因此,其收入是和平收入的三四倍。假设君主应该拥有,他所缺乏的立即增加收入的手段,以与其开支的增加相称;然而,必须从中提取增加收入的税收的产值,在征收这些税收之后的十到十二个月里,才开始进入国库。 但是,在战争开始的时刻,或者在战争似乎可能开始的时刻,必须增加军队,必须装备舰队,必须使守备的城镇处于防御状态;军队、舰队、这些守备的城镇必须配备武器、弹药和物资。 在眼前的危险时刻,必须立即支付巨额费用,这不会等待新税的逐步和缓慢的返还。 在这种紧急情况下,政府除了借贷之外,没有其他的资源。

p4.original: The same commercial state of society which, by the operation of moral causes, brings government in this manner into the necessity of borrowing, produces in the subjects both an ability and an inclination to lend. If it commonly brings along with it the necessity of borrowing, it likewise brings with it the facility of doing so.
p4.zh: 社会的商业状态,通过道德因素的运作,使政府以这种方式认识到借贷的必要性,在主体中产生借贷的能力和倾向。 如果它通常带来借款的必要性,它同样也带来这样做的便利。

p5.original: A country abounding with merchants and manufacturers, necessarily abounds with a set of people through whose hands, not only their own capitals, but the capitals of all those who either lend them money, or trust them with goods, pass as frequently, or more frequently, than the revenue of a private man, who, without trade or business, lives upon his income, passes through his hands. The revenue of such a man can regularly pass through his hands only once in a year. But the whole amount of the capital and credit of a merchant, who deals in a trade of which the returns are very quick, may sometimes pass through his hands two, three, or four times in a year. A country abounding with merchants and manufacturers, therefore, necessarily abounds with a set of people, who have it at all times in their power to advance, if they chuse to do so, a very large sum of money to government. Hence the ability in the subjects of a commercial state to lend.
p5.zh: 一个国家拥有众多的商人和制造商,必然有一群人,他们的手,不仅是他们自己的首都,而且是所有借钱或用货物信任他们的首都,比私人的收入频繁或更频繁地通过,而个人的收入,没有贸易或商业,靠自己的收入生活,就靠他的手。 这种人的收入一年只能定期通过他的手一次. 但是,一个商人的资本和信贷总额,如果交易的回报非常快,一年中有时可能通过他的双手两,三,四次. 因此,一个拥有众多商家和制造商的国家,必然拥有众多的人,他们随时可以推动,如果他们这样做,就给政府一笔非常大的资金。 因此,商业国家主体有能力提供贷款。

p6.original: Commerce and manufactures can seldom flourish long in any state which does not enjoy a regular administration of justice; in which the people do not feel themselves secure in the possession of their property; in which the faith of contracts is not supported by law; and in which the authority of the state is not supposed to be regularly employed in enforcing the payment of debts from all those who are able to pay. Commerce and manufactures, in short, can seldom flourish in any state, in which there is not a certain degree of confidence in the justice of government. The same confidence which disposes great merchants and manufacturers upon ordinary occasions, to trust their property to the protection of a particular government, disposes them, upon extraordinary occasions, to trust that government with the use of their property. By lending money to government, they do not even for a moment diminish their ability to carry on their trade and manufactures; on the contrary, they commonly augment it. The necessities of the state render government, upon most occasions willing to borrow upon terms extremely advantageous to the lender. The security which it grants to the original creditor, is made transferable to any other creditor; and from the universal confidence in the justice of the state, generally sells in the market for more than was originally paid for it. The merchant or monied man makes money by lending money to government, and instead of diminishing, increases his trading capital. He generally considers it as a favour, therefore, when the administration admits him to a share in the first subscription for a new loan. Hence the inclination or willingness in the subjects of a commercial state to lend.
p6.zh: 商业和制造业在没有正常司法的州很少能够长期繁荣;在州里,人民在拥有财产方面感到不安全;在州里,合同信仰得不到法律的支持;在州里,不应该经常利用国家权威来强制所有有能力支付的人支付债务。简言之,商业和制成品在任何一个国家都很少能够兴旺起来,在这些国家里,对政府的正义没有一定程度的信心. 在正常情况下,让大商人和制造商相信他们的财产受某一特定政府的保护,这种信心在非常情况下使他们相信该政府使用他们的财产。 通过向政府贷款,它们甚至一时不至于削弱它们继续其贸易和制造的能力;相反,它们通常会扩大这种能力。国家的需要使政府在大多数情况下愿意以对贷款人极为有利的条件借贷。 它给予原始债权人的担保可转让给任何其他债权人;从对国家司法的普遍信任来看,一般在市场上出售的金额超过原先所付的金额。商人或修道士通过向政府贷款来赚钱,而不是减少,而是增加他的贸易资本. 因此,他一般认为,当行政当局允许他在第一次订阅新贷款时,这是一种优惠。 因此,一个商业国家的主体有放款的倾向或意愿。

p7.original: The government of such a state is very apt to repose itself upon this ability and willingness of its subjects to lend it their money on extraordinary occasions. It foresees the facility of borrowing, and therefore dispenses itself from the duty of saving.
p7.zh: 这样一个国家的政府非常愿意依靠其臣民在非常情况下借钱的能力和意愿。 它预见到借贷便利,因此免除了储蓄的责任。

p8.original: In a rude state of society, there are no great mercantile or manufacturing capitals. The individuals, who hoard whatever money they can save, and who conceal their hoard, do so from a distrust of the justice of government; from a fear, that if it was known that they had a hoard, and where that hoard was to be found, they would quickly be plundered. In such a state of things, few people would be able, and nobody would be willing to lend their money to government on extraordinary exigencies. The sovereign feels that he must provide for such exigencies by saving, because he foresees the absolute impossibility of borrowing. This foresight increases still further his natural disposition to save.
p8.zh: 在社会粗鲁的状态下,没有大商贸或制造业的首都. 那些个人,他们囤积自己能节省的任何金钱,隐藏自己的囤积物,他们这样做是因为对政府正义的不信任;他们害怕,如果知道他们有囤积物,在那里会发现这种囤积物,他们就会很快被掠夺. 在这样的情况下,很少有人能够做到,没有人愿意在非常紧急的情况下把钱借给政府.君主认为,他必须通过储蓄来提供这种紧急需要,因为他预见到绝对不可能借贷。 这种预见使他更愿意自然地节省。

p9.original: The progress of the enormous debts which at present oppress, and will in the long-run probably ruin, all the great nations of Europe, has been pretty uniform. Nations, like private men, have generally begun to borrow upon what may be called personal credit, without assigning or mortgaging any particular fund for the payment of the debt; and when this resource has failed them, they have gone on to borrow upon assignments or mortgages of particular funds.
p9.zh: 目前压迫并可能长期破坏的巨额债务,即所有欧洲伟大国家,其进展相当一致。国家与私人一样,一般开始借取可称为个人信贷的贷款,而未分配或抵押任何特定基金以偿还债务;当这种资源使国家无力偿还债务时,它们就继续借取或抵押特定资金。

p10.original: What is called the unfunded debt of Great Britain, is contracted in the former of those two ways. It consists partly in a debt which bears, or is supposed to bear, no interest, and which resembles the debts that a private man contracts upon account; and partly in a debt which bears interest, and which resembles what a private man contracts upon his bill or promissory-note. The debts which are due, either for extraordinary services, or for services either not provided for, or not paid at the time when they are performed; part of the extraordinaries of the army, navy, and ordnance, the arrears of subsidies to foreign princes, those of seamen's wages, etc. usually constitute a debt of the first kind. Navy and exchequer bills, which are issued sometimes in payment of a part of such debts, and sometimes for other purposes, constitute a debt of the second kind; exchequer bills bearing interest from the day on which they are issued, and navy bills six months after they are issued. The bank of England, either by voluntarily discounting those bills at their current value, or by agreeing with government for certain considerations to circulate exchequer bills, that is, to receive them at par, paying the interest which happens to be due upon them, keeps up their value, and facilitates their circulation, and thereby frequently enables government to contract a very large debt of this kind. In France, where there is no bank, the state bills (billets d'etat {See Examen des Reflections Politiques sur les Finances.}) have sometimes sold at sixty and seventy per cent. discount. During the great recoinage in king William's time, when the bank of England thought proper to put a stop to its usual transactions, exchequer bills and tallies are said to have sold from twenty-five to sixty per cent. discount; owing partly, no doubt, to the supposed instability of the new government established by the Revolution, but partly, too, to the want of the support of the bank of England.
p10.zh: 所谓的大不列颠无资金的债务,就是以这两种方式中的前一种方式收缩的。部分债务包括不承担或理应承担利息的债务,类似私人所欠的债务;部分债务包括利息,类似私人根据账单或期票所订约的债务。应付的债款,有的用于特殊服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于特殊服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务;有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于服务,有的用于海军和国库账单有时是用来偿还部分债务,有时是用于其他目的,它们构成第二类债务;国库账单自发行之日起计息,海军账单自发行之日起计息,6个月后计息。英国银行要么自愿以现值贴现,要么与政府商定某些考虑,以流通财政票据,即按平价收取,支付恰好应该付给他们的利息,保持其价值,便利其流通,从而经常使政府能够签订非常大一笔这类债务。 在法国,没有银行,国家账单(billlet d'etat {见Examen des Reflections Politions sur les Finances.})有时以60%和70%的折扣出售。 在威廉国王时期的大重修期间,当英格兰银行认为应该停止其通常的交易时,据说财政账单和清点的售价从25%到60%不等. 折扣;毫无疑问,部分是由于革命建立的新政府的假定不稳定,但部分也是因为英格兰银行支持的匮乏.

p11.original: When this resource is exhausted, and it becomes necessary, in order to raise money, to assign or mortgage some particular branch of the public revenue for the payment of the debt, government has, upon different occasions, done this in two different ways. Sometimes it has made this assignment or mortgage for a short period of time only, a year, or a few years, for example; and sometimes for perpetuity. In the one case, the fund was supposed sufficient to pay, within the limited time, both principal and interest of the money borrowed. In the other, it was supposed sufficient to pay the interest only, or a perpetual annuity equivalent to the interest, government being at liberty to redeem, at any time, this annuity, upon paying back the principal sum borrowed. When money was raised in the one way, it was said to be raised by anticipation; when in the other, by perpetual funding, or, more shortly, by funding.
p11.zh: 当这种资源耗尽,而且为了筹集资金,有必要将公共收入的某个特定分支转让或抵押用于偿还债务时,政府在不同场合以两种不同的方式这样做。 有时,它只作短期、一年或几年的转让或抵押;有时是永久的。在一个案例中,基金应该足以在有限的时间内支付所借资金的本金和利息。 另一方面,政府只要还清借来的本金,就可以随时自由支付利息或相当于利息的永久年金,以赎回这一年金。一方面筹集资金,据说是通过预期筹集的;另一方面,通过长期供资,或很快通过供资筹集的。

p12.original: In Great Britain, the annual land and malt taxes are regularly anticipated every year, by virtue of a borrowing clause constantly inserted into the acts which impose them. The bank of England generally advances at an interest, which, since the Revolution, has varied from eight to three per cent., the sums of which those taxes are granted, and receives payment as their produce gradually comes in. If there is a deficiency, which there always is, it is provided for in the supplies of the ensuing year. The only considerable branch of the public revenue which yet remains unmortgaged, is thus regularly spent before it comes in. Like an improvident spendthrift, whose pressing occasions will not allow him to wait for the regular payment of his revenue, the state is in the constant practice of borrowing of its own factors and agents, and of paying interest for the use of its own money.
p12.zh: 在大不列颠,每年定期预期土地和麦芽税,因为借款条款经常被插入强加这些税项的法案中。英格兰银行一般以利息预付,自革命以来,利息从8%到3%不等。 发放这些税项的金额随着其产品逐步流入而得到付款。 如果存在缺陷,而缺陷始终存在,则在下一年的供给中予以规定。公共收入中唯一尚未摊销的相当一部分,因此在入库之前经常支出。国家就像一个不供应性开支者一样,其迫切的场合不允许他等待定期支付收入,而国家则在不断的习惯上借用自己的因素和代理人,并支付使用自己的钱的利息.

p13.original: In the reign of king William, and during a great part of that of queen Anne, before we had become so familiar as we are now with the practice of perpetual funding, the greater part of the new taxes were imposed but for a short period of time (for four, five, six, or seven years only), and a great part of the grants of every year consisted in loans upon anticipations of the produce of those taxes. The produce being frequently insufficient for paying, within the limited term, the principal and interest of the money borrowed, deficiencies arose; to make good which, it became necessary to prolong the term.
p13.zh: 在威廉王的统治中,在安妮王后的大部分统治中,在我们开始像现在这样熟悉永久资助的做法之前,新税的很大一部分是强加的,但时间很短(只有四、五、六或七年),每年的赠款中很大一部分是在预期这些税的产物时提供的贷款。产品往往不足以在有限期限内支付所借资金的本金和利息,因此出现了缺陷;为了达到目的,必须延长期限。

p14.original: In 1697, by the 8th of William III., c. 20, the deficiencies of several taxes were charged upon what was then called the first general mortgage or fund, consisting of a prolongation to the first of August 1706, of several different taxes, which would have expired within a shorter term, and of which the produce was accumulated into one general fund. The deficiencies charged upon this prolonged term amounted to £5,160,459: 14: 9½.
p14.zh: 1697年,到威廉三世第八世时,c.20,数项税的缺陷被征收到当时所谓的第一笔一般抵押贷款或基金上,包括将数项不同的税费延长到1706年8月1日,这些税费在较短的期限内到期,其中的产物被累积为一个普通基金. 这一长期期间的缺陷达5,160,459英镑:14:91⁄2。

p15.original: In 1701, those duties, with some others, were still further prolonged, for the like purposes, till the first of August 1710, and were called the second general mortgage or fund. The deficiencies charged upon it amounted to £2,055,999: 7: 11½.
p15.zh: 1701年,这些职责,以及其他一些职责,出于类似目的,仍然被进一步延长,直到1710年8月1日,并被称为第二次一般抵押贷款或基金. 对它收取的缺陷达2,055,999英镑:7:111⁄2.

p16.original: In 1707, those duties were still further prolonged, as a fund for new loans, to the first of August 1712, and were called the third general mortgage or fund. The sum borrowed upon it was £983,254:11:9¼.
p16.zh: 1707年,作为新贷款基金,这些职责仍被进一步延长至1712年8月1日,并被称为第三次一般抵押贷款或基金.借给它的钱是983,254英镑:11:91⁄4.

p17.original: In 1708, those duties were all (except the old subsidy of tonnage and poundage, of which one moiety only was made a part of this fund, and a duty upon the importation of Scotch linen, which had been taken off by the articles of union) still further continued, as a fund for new loans, to the first of August 1714, and were called the fourth general mortgage or fund. The sum borrowed upon it was £925,176:9:2¼.
p17.zh: 1708年,这些责任全部(除了吨位和磅位的旧补贴,其中只有一笔小钱是这笔基金的一部分,以及进口被工会条款取消的苏格兰亚麻布的一项义务),作为新贷款基金,一直持续到1714年8月1日,并称为第四笔一般抵押贷款或基金。借给它的钱是925,176英镑:9:21⁄4。

p18.original: In 1709, those duties were all ( except the old subsidy of tonnage and poundage, which was now left out of this fund altogether ) still further continued, for the same purpose, to the first of August 1716, and were called the fifth general mortgage or fund. The sum borrowed upon it was £922,029:6s.
p18.zh: 1709年,这些职责全部(除了吨位和磅位的旧补贴,现在完全从这个基金中被排除在外),为了同样的目的,继续延续到1716年8月1日,并被称为第五个一般抵押贷款或基金。借给它的钱是922,029:6英镑。

p19.original: In 1710, those duties were again prolonged to the first of August 1720, and were called the sixth general mortgage or fund. The sum borrowed upon it was £1,296,552:9:11¾.
p19.zh: 1710年,这些职责再次被延长至1720年8月1日,并被称为第六普通抵押贷款或基金.借给它的钱是1,296,552:9:113⁄4英镑。

p20.original: In 1711, the same duties (which at this time were thus subject to four different anticipations), together with several others, were continued for ever, and made a fund for paying the interest of the capital of the South-sea company, which had that year advanced to government, for paying debts, and making good deficiencies, the sum of £9,177,967:15:4d, the greatest loan which at that time had ever been made.
p20.zh: 1711年,同样的职责(因此目前有四个不同的预期),加上其他几个职责,一直延续至今,并且为支付当年提前到政府的南海公司资本利息,偿还债务,以及弥补好亏,9,177,967:15:4d英镑,这是当时贷款最多的一笔资金.

p21.original: Before this period, the principal, so far as I have been able to observe, the only taxes, which, in order to pay the interest of a debt, had been imposed for perpetuity, were those for paying the interest of the money which had been advanced to government by the bank and East-India company, and of what it was expected would be advanced, but which was never advanced, by a projected land bank. The bank fund at this time amounted to £3,375,027:17:10½, for which was paid an annuity or interest of £206,501:15:5d. The East-India fund amounted to £3,200,000, for which was paid an annuity or interest of £160,000; the bank fund being at six per cent., the East-India fund at five per cent. interest.
p21.zh: 在此之前,本金,就我所能观察到的,唯一为了偿还债务利息而征收的税,是永久的,是支付银行和东印度公司向政府垫付的款项的利息的税,是预期的,是预付的,但从未预付的,是由预计的陆上银行垫付的.此时的银行基金达到3,375,027:17:101⁄2英镑,为此支付的年金或利息为206,501:15:5d英镑.东印度基金为3,200,000英镑,为此支付了160,000英镑的年金或利息;银行基金为6%,东印度基金为5%。

p22.original: In 1715, by the first of George I., c. 12, the different taxes which had been mortgaged for paying the bank annuity, together with several others, which, by this act, were likewise rendered perpetual, were accumulated into one common fund, called the aggregate fund, which was charged not only with the payment of the bank annuity, but with several other annuities and burdens of different kinds. This fund was afterwards augmented by the third of George I., c.8., and by the fifth of George I., c. 3, and the different duties which were then added to it were likewise rendered perpetual.
p22.zh: 1715年,由乔治一世第一位,c.12,为支付银行年金而抵押的不同税项,连同其他若干项税项,根据这项法令,这些税项同样是永久性的,被累积为一个共同基金,即总基金,它不仅收取银行年金的支付费用,而且还承担若干其他各种年金和负担。该基金后来又增加了乔治一世的三分之一,c.8.,以及乔治一世的五分之一,c.。3, 以及后来增加的不同职责也同样被永久化。

p23.original: In 1717, by the third of George I., c. 7, several other taxes were rendered perpetual, and accumulated into another common fund, called the general fund, for the payment of certain annuities, amounting in the whole to £724,849:6:10½.
p23.zh: 1717年,由乔治一世的第三任,c.7,其他几种税收被永久化,积累成另一个共同基金,即普通基金,以支付某些年金,共计724,849英镑:6:101⁄2.

p24.original: In consequence of those different acts, the greater part of the taxes, which before had been anticipated only for a short term of years were rendered perpetual, as a fund for paying, not the capital, but the interest only, of the money which had been borrowed upon them by different successive anticipations.
p24.zh: 由于这些不同的行为,以前只预计到短期的税收大部分将永久化,作为支付资金,而不是资本,而仅仅是通过不同的连续预期而借给他们的资金的利息。

p25.original: Had money never been raised but by anticipation, the course of a few years would have liberated the public revenue, without any other attention of government besides that of not overloading the fund, by charging it with more debt than it could pay within the limited term, and not of anticipating a second time before the expiration of the first anticipation. But the greater part of European governments have been incapable of those attentions. They have frequently overloaded the fund, even upon the first anticipation; and when this happened not to be the case, they have generally taken care to overload it, by anticipating a second and a third time, before the expiration of the first anticipation. The fund becoming in this manner altogether insufficient for paying both principal and interest of the money borrowed upon it, it became necessary to charge it with the interest only, or a perpetual annuity equal to the interest; and such improvident anticipations necessarily gave birth to the more ruinous practice of perpetual funding. But though this practice necessarily puts off the liberation of the public revenue from a fixed period, to one so indefinite that it is not very likely ever to arrive; yet, as a greater sum can, in all cases, be raised by this new practice than by the old one of anticipation, the former, when men have once become familiar with it, has, in the great exigencies of the state, been universally preferred to the latter. To relieve the present exigency, is always the object which principally interests those immediately concerned in the administration of public affairs. The future liberation of the public revenue they leave to the care of posterity.
p25.zh: 如果资金从未筹集到,但是通过预期,几年的路程本来可以解放公共收入,除了政府不给基金过多的任何其他关注之外,还可以向基金收取超出其有限期限所能支付的债务,而不是在第一次预期到期前第二次预测。 但大部分欧洲政府都未能重视这些问题。 他们经常超负荷使用基金,甚至在第一次预期时也是如此;当情况并非如此时,他们通常会注意超负荷使用基金,在第一次预期到期前,他们会预测第二次和第三次。基金变得完全不足以支付所借资金的本金和利息,因此必须只收取利息,或支付与利息相等的永久年金;这种不成熟的预期必然导致更毁灭性的永久供资做法。 但是,虽然这种做法必然使公共收入从固定时期解放到一个如此无限期,以致不可能到达;但是,由于这种新做法总能比原先的预期做法筹集到更大的数额,因此,当男子一度熟悉时,在国家极为紧急的情况下,人们普遍倾向于后者。解除目前的紧急需要,始终是那些与公共事务管理直接有关的人主要关心的目标。将来公共收入的解放,留给后代照顾。

p26.original: During the reign of queen Anne, the market rate of interest had fallen from six to five per cent.; and, in the twelfth year of her reign, five per cent. was declared to be the highest rate which could lawfully be taken for money borrowed upon private security. Soon after the greater part of the temporary taxes of Great Britain had been rendered perpetual, and distributed into the aggregate, South-sea, and general funds, the creditors of the public, like those of private persons, were induced to accept of five per cent. for the interest of their money, which occasioned a saving of one per cent. upon the capital of the greater part or the debts which had been thus funded for perpetuity, or of one-sixth of the greater part of the annuities which were paid out of the three great funds above mentioned. This saving left a considerable surplus in the produce of the different taxes which had been accumulated into those funds, over and above what was necessary for paying the annuities which were now charged upon them, and laid the foundation of what has since been called the sinking fund. In 1717, it amounted to £523,454:7:7½. In 1727, the interest of the greater part of the public debts was still further reduced to four per cent.; and, in 1753 and 1757, to three and a-half, and three per cent., which reductions still further augmented the sinking fund.
p26.zh: 在安妮王后统治期间,市场利率从6%降至5%;在安妮王后统治的第十二年,5%被宣布为可合法用于私人证券借款的最高利率。 在大不列颠临时税收的大部分被永久化并分配给总的、南海的和一般的基金之后不久,公共债权人,如私人债权人,就为了其资金的利益,被迫接受5%的利息,从而节省了1%的资本,或永久获得资金的债务,或上述三大基金中支付的年金的六分之一。 这一节省使这些基金积累起来的各种税收的产量有相当的盈余,超出支付现在由它们支付的年金所必须的数额,并为后来所谓的沉没基金奠定了基础。1717年,达到523,454英镑:7:71⁄2.1727年,大部分公共债务的利息进一步降至4%;1753年和1757年,又降至3.5和3%,这进一步增加了下沉基金.

p27.original: A sinking fund, though instituted for the payment of old, facilitates very much the contracting of new debts. It is a subsidiary fund, always at hand, to be mortgaged in aid of any other doubtful fund, upon which money is proposed to be raised in any exigency of the state. Whether the sinking fund of Great Britain has been more frequently applied to the one or to other of those two purposes, will sufficiently appear by and by.
p27.zh: 一项沉没基金虽然是为偿还旧债而设立的,但大大便利了新债务的订约。 它是一个附属基金,始终处于手头,要抵押给任何其他可疑基金,提议在国家任何紧急需要时,用它来筹集资金。 大不列颠的沉没基金是否更经常地用于这两种目的中的一种或另一种目的,将充分显现出来。

p28.original: Besides those two methods of borrowing, by anticipations and by a perpetual funding, there are two other methods, which hold a sort of middle place between them; these are, that of borrowing upon annuities for terms of years, and that of borrowing upon annuities for lives.
p28.zh: 除了这两种借贷方式之外,还有两种其他方式,即通过预期和长期供资,在两者之间占有某种中位位置;这两种方式是,按年金借款,和按年金借款。

p29.original: During the reigns of king William and queen Anne, large sums were frequently borrowed upon annuities for terms of years, which were sometimes longer and sometimes shorter. In 1695, an act was passed for borrowing one million upon an annuity of fourteen per cent., or £140,000 a-year, for sixteen years. In 1691, an act was passed for borrowing a million upon annuities for lives, upon terms which, in the present times, would appear very advantageous; but the subscription was not filled up. In the following year, the deficiency was made good, by borrowing upon annuities for lives, at fourteen per cent. or a little more than seven years purchase. In 1695, the persons who had purchased those annuities were allowed to exchange them for others of ninety-six years, upon paying into the exchequer sixty-three pounds in the hundred; that is, the difference between fourteen per cent. for life, and fourteen per cent. for ninety-six years, was sold for sixty-three pounds, or for four and a-half years purchase. Such was the supposed instability of government, that even these terms procured few purchasers. In the reign of queen Anne, money was, upon different occasions, borrowed both upon annuities for lives, and upon annuities for terms of thirty-two, of eighty-nine, of ninety-eight, and of ninety-nine years. In 1719, the proprietors of the annuities for thirty-two years were induced to accept, in lieu of them, South-sea stock to the amount of eleven and a-half years purchase of the annuities, together with an additional quantity of stock, equal to the arrears which happened then to be due upon them. In 1720, the greater part of the other annuities for terms of years, both long and short, were subscribed into the same fund. The long annuities, at that time, amounted to £666,821: 8:3½ a-year. On the 5th of January 1775, the remainder of them, or what was not subscribed at that time, amounted only to £136,453:12:8d.
p29.zh: 在威廉王和安妮王后统治时期,大笔款项经常借在年金上借到,这些年金有时更长,有时更短.1695年,通过了一项法案,规定以14%的年金(即每年140 000英镑)借款100万,为期16年。1691年,通过了一项法案,规定终身借100万年金,在目前看来,这一条件非常有利;但订阅额没有填满。 次年,通过终身借入年金,弥补了短缺,为14%,或略多于七年。1695年,购买这些年金的人,在缴入百年税金后,允许他们换回其他九十六年的年金;即终身的差额为14%.,九十六年的年金为六十三斤,或四年半的年金为购买. 这就是所谓的政府不稳定,即使这些条件也采购了很少的购买者。 在安妮王后统治时期,钱款在不同场合上借入终身年金,以及三十二年,八十九年,九十八年,九十九年的年金.1719年,32年年金的拥有者被诱使接受11年半的南海股票购买年金,加上额外数量的股票,相当于当时发生的拖欠款项。1720年,其他年金的大部分,无论是长的还是短的,都加入了同一基金。 当时的长年金达到666,821:每年8:31⁄2英镑.1775年1月5日,其余的,或当时尚未订阅的,仅达136,453英镑:12:8d.

p30.original: During the two wars which began in 1739 and in 1755, little money was borrowed, either upon annuities for terms of years, or upon those for lives. An annuity for ninety-eight or ninety-nine years, however, is worth nearly as much as a perpetuity, and should therefore, one might think, be a fund for borrowing nearly as much. But those who, in order to make family settlements, and to provide for remote futurity, buy into the public stocks, would not care to purchase into one of which the value was continually diminishing; and such people make a very considerable proportion, both of the proprietors and purchasers of stock. An annuity for a long term of years, therefore, though its intrinsic value may be very nearly the same with that of a perpetual annuity, will not find nearly the same number of purchasers. The subscribers to a new loan, who mean generally to sell their subscription as soon as possible, prefer greatly a perpetual annuity, redeemable by parliament, to an irredeemable annuity, for a long term of years, of only equal amount. The value of the former may be supposed always the same, or very nearly the same; and it makes, therefore, a more convenient transferable stock than the latter.
p30.zh: 在1739年和1755年开始的两次战争中,借到很少的钱,要么是按年计年金,要么是按生命计年金。 然而,九十八年或九十九年的年金几乎相当于永久的年金,因此,人们可能认为,是几乎同样多的借款基金。 但是,那些为了建立家庭定居点和提供遥远的未来而购买公共股票的人,并不想购买价值不断下降的股票;这些人在股票的拥有者和购买者中占有相当大的比例。 因此,虽然年金的内在价值可能与永久年金的内在价值几乎相同,但购买者的数目却几乎相同。新的贷款的订户一般是尽快出售其认购的,他们更喜欢议会可以赎回的永久年金,而更喜欢长期只有同等数额的不可弥补年金。前者的价值可能总是相同的,或者几乎是相同的;因此,它使可转让的股票比后者更方便。

p31.original: During the two last-mentioned wars, annuities, either for terms of years or for lives, were seldom granted, but as premiums to the subscribers of a new loan, over and above the redeemable annuity or interest, upon the credit of which the loan was supposed to be made. They were granted, not as the proper fund upon which the money was borrowed, but as an additional encouragement to the lender.
p31.zh: 在最后两次战争期间,很少发放年金或终身年金,但作为新贷款的订户的保险费,其数额超过可赎回的年金或利息,而这笔贷款本应从这些年金或利息中贷出。 这些贷款不是作为借款的适当基金发放的,而是作为对贷款人的额外鼓励。

p32.original: Annuities for lives have occasionally been granted in two different ways; either upon separate lives, or upon lots of lives, which, in French, are called tontines, from the name of their inventor. When annuities are granted upon separate lives, the death of every individual annuitant disburdens the public revenue, so far as it was affected by his annuity. When annuities are granted upon tontines, the liberation of the public revenue does not commence till the death of all the annuitants comprehended in one lot, which may sometimes consist of twenty or thirty persons, of whom the survivors succeed to the annuities of all those who die before them; the last survivor succeeding to the annuities of the whole lot. Upon the same revenue, more money can always be raised by tontines than by annuities for separate lives. An annuity, with a right of survivorship, is really worth more than an equal annuity for a separate life; and, from the confidence which every man naturally has in his own good fortune, the principle upon which is founded the success of all lotteries, such an annuity generally sells for something more than it is worth. In countries where it is usual for government to raise money by granting annuities, tontines are, upon this account, generally preferred to annuities for separate lives. The expedient which will raise most money, is almost always preferred to that which is likely to bring about, in the speediest manner, the liberation of the public revenue.
p32.zh: 生命的年金偶尔会以两种不同的方式授予;或者在分开的生活上,或者在很多生命上,在法语中,这些生命从发明人的名字中被称为丰提(tontines). 如果在单独生活时发放年金,每个年金人的死亡都会给公共收入带来负担,只要其年金受到影响。 当给丰地人发放年金时,公共收入的解放要等到所有被理解为一票的年金的人死亡时才会开始,这些年金有时可能包括20或30人,其中幸存者继承了所有在他们之前去世者的年金;最后的幸存者继承了全部年金。 在相同收入的基础上,丰地人总是可以筹集更多的钱,而不是为分开的生活而领取年金。年金,有生存权,真正值的不仅仅是一个单独的生活中的同等年金;而且,从每个人自然对自己的好运气的信心来看,这个原则是所有彩票的成功的基础,这种年金一般以比它更值钱的东西出售。 在政府通常通过发放年金来筹集资金的国家,根据这一说法,一般宁可将各年的年金分开。筹集大部分资金的权宜之计,几乎总是比以最快方式释放公共收入的权宜之计更为可取。

p33.original: In France, a much greater proportion of the public debts consists in annuities for lives than in England. According to a memoir presented by the parliament of Bourdeaux to the king, in 1764, the whole public debt of France is estimated at twenty-four hundred millions of livres; of which the capital, for which annuities for lives had been granted, is supposed to amount to three hundred millions, the eighth part of the whole public debt. The annuities themselves are computed to amount to thirty millions a-year, the fourth part of one hundred and twenty millions, the supposed interest of that whole debt. These estimations, I know very well, are not exact; but having been presented by so very respectable a body as approximations to the truth, they may, I apprehend, be considered as such. It is not the different degrees of anxiety in the two governments of France and England for the liberation of the public revenue, which occasions this difference in their respective modes of borrowing; it arises altogether from the different views and interests of the lenders.
p33.zh: 在法国,公共债务中包括终身年金的比例远高于英国。 根据波尔多议会向国王提交的回忆录,1764年,法国的全部公债估计达2.4亿里弗;其中首都,已获得终身年金,应达3亿,是整个公债的第八部分.年金本身计算为每年3 000万年,即1.2亿年中的第四部分,即所谓的全部债务利息。 我非常清楚地知道,这些估计并不准确;但是,一个非常受人尊敬的机构提出了与真相相近的估计数,我认为,这些估计数可能被视为事实。 法国和英格兰两国政府对解放公共收入的焦虑程度不同,这在它们各自的借贷方式上都表明了这种不同;这完全产生于放款人的不同观点和利益.

p34.original: In England, the seat of government being in the greatest mercantile city in the world, the merchants are generally the people who advance money to government. By advancing it, they do not mean to diminish, but, on the contrary, to increase their mercantile capitals; and unless they expected to sell, with some profit, their share in the subscription for a new loan, they never would subscribe. But if, by advancing their money, they were to purchase, instead of perpetual annuities, annuities for lives only, whether their own or those of other people, they would not always be so likely to sell them with a profit. Annuities upon their own lives they would always sell with loss; because no man will give for an annuity upon the life of another, whose age and state of health are nearly the same with his own, the same price which he would give for one upon his own. An annuity upon the life of a third person, indeed, is, no doubt, of equal value to the buyer and the seller; but its real value begins to diminish from the moment it is granted, and continues to do so, more and more, as long as it subsists. It can never, therefore, make so convenient a transferable stock as a perpetual annuity, of which the real value may be supposed always the same, or very nearly the same.
p34.zh: 在英国,政府所在地位于世界上最繁华的商贸城市,商人一般是向政府提款的人. 通过推进,它们并不意味着减少,而是相反地增加它们的商贸资本;除非它们期望以一定利润出售它们在新贷款的认购中的份额,否则它们永远不会认购. 但是,如果通过提款,他们购买的年金不是永久的年金,而是仅仅购买他们自己的年金,或者购买其他人的年金,那么他们就未必总能以利润出售这些年金。 他们一生的年金总是亏损地出售;因为没有人会给另一个人的年金,而另一个人的年金和健康状况与他自己几乎相同,与他自己给一个人的年金一样。 事实上,第三人寿的年金无疑对买方和卖方具有同等价值;但是,其实际价值从给予时起开始减少,而且只要其继续存在,这种价值就会增加。 因此,它永远不能将可转让的股票作为永久年金,而实际价值可能总是一样或几乎一样。

p35.original: In France, the seat of government not being in a great mercantile city, merchants do not make so great a proportion of the people who advance money to government. The people concerned in the finances, the farmers-general, the receivers of the taxes which are not in farm, the court-bankers, etc. make the greater part of those who advance their money in all public exigencies. Such people are commonly men of mean birth, but of great wealth, and frequently of great pride. They are too proud to marry their equals, and women of quality disdain to marry them. They frequently resolve, therefore, to live bachelors; and having neither any families of their own, nor much regard for those of their relations, whom they are not always very fond of acknowledging, they desire only to live in splendour during their own time, and are not unwilling that their fortune should end with themselves. The number of rich people, besides, who are either averse to marry, or whose condition of life renders it either improper or inconvenient for them to do so, is much greater in France than in England. To such people, who have little or no care for posterity, nothing can be more convenient than to exchange their capital for a revenue, which is to last just as long, and no longer, than they wish it to do.
p35.zh: 在法国,政府所在地不是在大商贸城市,商人并不给向政府提款的人带来如此大的比例.财政相关人员,农民总务人员,不在农场的税收接收人员,法院银行等,使在一切公共应急中垫付资金的占较大比例.这些人通常都是出身卑微,但财富巨大,而且常常引以为豪。 她们太骄傲了,不能与她们平等结婚,而那些有品格的蔑视妇女却不愿与她们结婚。 因此,他们常常决心要活单身汉;他们既没有自己的任何家庭,也没有非常关心他们关系上的家庭,他们并不总是很喜欢承认这些家庭,他们只希望在他们自己的时间里过着丰盛的生活,也不不愿意他们的命运与自己结束。 此外,法国的富人要么不愿意结婚,要么其生活条件使他们不适当或不方便结婚,比英国要多得多。 对于这种人,对后世几乎不关心或根本不关心,没有什么比用资本换取收入更方便的了,收入的维持时间是一样长的,没有比他们希望的更长的.

p36.original: The ordinary expense of the greater part of modern governments, in time of peace, being equal, or nearly equal, to their ordinary revenue, when war comes, they are both unwilling and unable to increase their revenue in proportion to the increase of their expense. They are unwilling, for fear of offending the people, who, by so great and so sudden an increase of taxes, would soon be disgusted with the war; and they are unable, from not well knowing what taxes would be sufficient to produce the revenue wanted. The facility of borrowing delivers them from the embarrassment which this fear and inability would otherwise occasion. By means of borrowing, they are enabled, with a very moderate increase of taxes, to raise, from year to year, money sufficient for carrying on the war; and by the practice of perpetual funding, they are enabled, with the smallest possible increase of taxes, to raise annually the largest possible sum of money. In great empires, the people who live in the capital, and in the provinces remote from the scene of action, feel, many of them, scarce any inconveniency from the war, but enjoy, at their ease, the amusement of reading in the newspapers the exploits of their own fleets and armies. To them this amusement compensates the small difference between the taxes which they pay on account of the war, and those which they had been accustomed to pay in time of peace. They are commonly dissatisfied with the return of peace, which puts an end to their amusement, and to a thousand visionary hopes of conquest and national glory, from a longer continuance of the war.
p36.zh: 现代政府大部分的普通开支,在和平时期,与普通收入相等,或几乎相等,在战争到来时,他们既不愿意,又不能按照支出增加的比例增加收入. 他们不愿意,因为害怕冒犯人民,由于如此巨大和突然增加税收,人民很快会因战争而厌恶;他们也因为不知道什么税收足以产生所希望的收入而不能这样做。借钱的便利使他们摆脱了这种恐惧和无力本来会带来的尴尬。 通过借贷,他们能够每年筹集到足以维持战争的资金,税收增加幅度很小;通过长期供资的做法,他们能够每年筹集到尽可能多的资金,税收增加幅度最小。 在大帝国中,生活在首都和远离行动现场的省份的人民,感到,其中许多人很少受到战争的不便,但轻松地享受报纸上阅读他们自己的舰队和军队的剥削的乐趣。对他们来说,这种娱乐弥补了他们因战争而缴纳的税款与他们在和平时期习惯缴纳的税款之间的微小差别。 他们通常对和平的恢复感到不满,因为和平结束了他们的娱乐,对从战争持续时间更长的意义上来说,对征服和民族荣耀的一千个有远见的希望感到不满。

p37.original: The return of peace, indeed, seldom relieves them from the greater part of the taxes imposed during the war. These are mortgaged for the interest of the debt contracted, in order to carry it on. If, over and above paying the interest of this debt, and defraying the ordinary expense of government, the old revenue, together with the new taxes, produce some surplus revenue, it may, perhaps, be converted into a sinking fund for paying off the debt. But, in the first place, this sinking fund, even supposing it should be applied to no other purpose, is generally altogether inadequate for paying, in the course of any period during which it can reasonably be expected that peace should continue, the whole debt contracted during the war; and, in the second place, this fund is almost always applied to other purposes.
p37.zh: 事实上,恢复和平很少解除战争期间征收的大部分税。 这些债务是按合同债务利息抵押的,以便继续偿还。 如果除了支付这笔债务的利息,并支付政府的普通开支之外,旧收入连同新的税收,产生一些盈余收入,也许可以转换成偿还债务的沉没基金. 但是,首先,这一沉没基金,即使假定它不应用于任何其他目的,一般也完全不足以支付战争期间可以合理预期和平会继续下去的任何期间的全部债务;其次,这一基金几乎总是用于其他目的。

p38.original: The new taxes were imposed for the sole purpose of paying the interest of the money borrowed upon them. If they produce more, it is generally something which was neither intended nor expected, and is, therefore, seldom very considerable. Sinking funds have generally arisen, not so much from any surplus of the taxes which was over and above what was necessary for paying the interest or annuity originally charged upon them, as from a subsequent reduction of that interest; that of Holland in 1655, and that of the ecclesiastical state in 1685, were both formed in this manner. Hence the usual insufficiency of such funds.
p38.zh: 征收新税的唯一目的是支付借给他们的钱的利息。 如果生产更多,一般说来,它不是有意的,也不是预期的,因此很少是相当可观的。 一般说来,沉没资金来自税收的盈余,这些盈余超过支付原先收取的利息或年金所必需的数额,而后来由于利息的减少;荷兰1655年的利息和教会国家1685年的利息都是以这种方式形成的。 因此,这种资金通常不足。

p39.original: During the most profound peace, various events occur, which require an extraordinary expense; and government finds it always more convenient to defray this expense by misapplying the sinking fund, than by imposing a new tax. Every new tax is immediately felt more or less by the people. It occasions always some murmur, and meets with some opposition. The more taxes may have been multiplied, the higher they may have been raised upon every different subject of taxation; the more loudly the people complain of every new tax, the more difficult it becomes, too, either to find out new subjects of taxation, or to raise much higher the taxes already imposed upon the old. A momentary suspension of the payment of debt is not immediately felt by the people, and occasions neither murmur nor complaint. To borrow of the sinking fund is always an obvious and easy expedient for getting out of the present difficulty. The more the public debts may have been accumulated, the more necessary it may have become to study to reduce them; the more dangerous, the more ruinous it may be to misapply any part of the sinking fund; the less likely is the public debt to be reduced to any considerable degree, the more likely, the more certainly, is the sinking fund to be misapplied towards defraying all the extraordinary expenses which occur in time of peace. When a nation is already overburdened with taxes, nothing but the necessities of a new war, nothing but either the animosity of national vengeance, or the anxiety for national security, can induce the people to submit, with tolerable patience, to a new tax. Hence the usual misapplication of the sinking fund.
p39.zh: 在最深刻的和平时期,发生了各种事件,这需要特别的开支;政府发现,通过错误使用沉没基金来支付这笔开支总是比征收新税更方便。 每一次新税,人民立即或多或少地感受到. 它总是有些喃喃自语,并遇到一些反对者。征税额越多,对每个不同的征税对象征收的税额可能越高;人民对每一新税额的抱怨越响亮,就越难找到新的征税对象,或者提高已经加给老的税额.人民没有立即感到暂时中止债务的支付,而且有时既不喃喃也不抱怨。借下沉基金总是摆脱目前困难的明显和容易的方便。公共债务的积累越多,就越有必要研究减少这些债务;越是危险,越是破坏,误用沉没基金的任何部分;公共债务减少到任何相当程度的可能性就越小,越是可能,更肯定的是,沉没基金被误用于支付和平时期发生的所有非常费用。 当一个国家已经负担过重的税收,只有一场新战争的需要,只有对国家复仇的敌意,或对国家安全的焦虑,才能促使人民以容忍的耐心接受新的税收。 因此,沉船基金通常被误用。

p40.original: In Great Britain, from the time that we had first recourse to the ruinous expedient of perpetual funding, the reduction of the public debt, in time of peace, has never borne any proportion to its accumulation in time of war. It was in the war which began in 1668, and was concluded by the treaty of Ryswick, in 1697, that the foundation of the present enormous debt of Great Britain was first laid.
p40.zh: 在大不列颠,从我们第一次诉诸于永久资金的毁灭性手段之时起,在和平时期减少公共债务从未在战争时期承担过任何部分的积累。 正是在1668年开始的战争中,在1697年赖斯威克条约下达成,大不列颠目前巨额债务的基础首先奠定.

p41.original: On the 31st of December 1697, the public debts of Great Britain, funded and unfunded, amounted to £21,515,742:13:8½. A great part of those debts had been contracted upon short anticipations, and some part upon annuities for lives; so that, before the 31st of December 1701, in less than four years, there had partly been paid off; and partly reverted to the public, the sum of £5,121,041:12:0¾d; a greater reduction of the public debt than has ever since been brought about in so short a period of time. The remaining debt, therefore, amounted only to £16,394,701:1:7¼d.
p41.zh: 1697年12月31日,大不列颠国公债务,资金筹足,资金无着落,达21,515,742:13:81⁄2. 这些债务中很大一部分是短期预期债务,部分是终身年金;因此,在1701年12月31日之前,不到四年的时间里,部分债务就得到了偿还;部分还给了公众5,121,041:12:03⁄4d英镑;比此后在如此短的时间内实现更大的公共债务减少。 因此,剩余的债务仅达16 394 701英镑:1 71⁄4d。

p42.original: In the war which began in 1702, and which was concluded by the treaty of Utrecht, the public debts were still more accumulated. On the 31st of December 1714, they amounted to £53,681,076:5:6½. The subscription into the South-sea fund, of the short and long annuities, increased the capital of the public debt; so that, on the 31st of December 1722, it amounted to £55,282,978:1:3 5/6. The reduction of the debt began in 1723, and went on so slowly, that, on the 31st of December 1739, during seventeen years-of profound peace, the whole sum paid off was no more than £8,328,554:17:11 3/12, the capital of the public debt, at that time, amounting to £46,954,623:3:4 7/12.
p42.zh: 在1702年开始的由乌得勒支条约缔结的战争中,公共债务的积累仍然较多.1714年12月31日,达到53,681,076:5:61⁄2英镑.入南海基金,收纳短年和长年,增加了公债资本;因此,1722年12月31日,公债资本达到55,282,978英镑:1:3 5/6.减债始于1723年,持续得如此缓慢,以至于1739年12月31日,在十七年的深刻安宁中,全部还清的金额不超过8,328,554:17:11 3/12英镑,是当时公债的资本,共计46,954,623:3:4 7/12英镑.

p43.original: The Spanish war, which began in 1739, and the French war which soon followed it, occasioned a further increase of the debt, which, on the 31st of December 1748, after the war had been concluded by the treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, amounted to £78,293,313:1:10¾. The most profound peace, of 17 years continuance, had taken no more than £8,328,354, 17:11¼ from it. A war, of less than nine years continuance, added £31,338,689:18: 6 1/6 to it. {See James Postlethwaite's History of the Public Revenue.}
p43.zh: 1739年开始的西班牙战争,以及随即发生的法国战争,使得债务进一步增加,在阿伊克斯-拉-查佩尔条约缔结战争后的1748年12月31日,债务达到78,293,313英镑:1:103⁄4.持续17年的最深远的和平,只花了8 328 354英镑,17:111⁄4英镑。一场持续不到九年的战争,增加了31,338,689:18英镑:6 1/6. {见詹姆斯·波斯特莱特华特的公共收入史。 }

p44.original: During the administration of Mr. Pelham, the interest of the public debt was reduced, or at least measures were taken for reducing it, from four to three per cent.; the sinking fund was increased, and some part of the public debt was paid off. In 1755, before the breaking out of the late war, the funded debt of Great Britain amounted to £72,289,675. On the 5th of January 1763, at the conclusion of the peace, the funded debt amounted debt to £122,603,336:8:2¼. The unfunded debt has been stated at £13,927,589:2:2. But the expense occasioned by the war did not end with the conclusion of the peace; so that, though on the 5th of January 1764, the funded debt was increased (partly by a new loan, and partly by funding a part of the unfunded debt) to £129,586,789:10:1¾, there still remained (according to the very well informed author of Considerations on the Trade and Finances of Great Britain) an unfunded debt, which was brought to account in that and the following year, of £9,975,017: 12:2 15/44d. In 1764, therefore, the public debt of Great Britain, funded and unfunded together, amounted, according to this author, to £139,561,807:2:4. The annuities for lives, too, which had been granted as premiums to the subscribers to the new loans in 1757, estimated at fourteen years purchase, were valued at £472,500; and the annuities for long terms of years, granted as premiums likewise, in 1761 and 1762, estimated at twenty-seven and a-half years purchase, were valued at £6,826,875. During a peace of about seven years continuance, the prudent and truly patriotic administration of Mr. Pelham was not able to pay off an old debt of six millions. During a war of nearly the same continuance, a new debt of more than seventy-five millions was contracted.
p44.zh: 在对Mr. 先生的执政期间Pelham, 公共债务利息减少,或至少采取措施将其从4%降至3%;沉没基金增加,部分公共债务得到偿还.1755年,在晚期战争爆发前,英国的资金债务达到72,289,675英镑.1763年1月5日,和平结束,注资债务达到122,603,336英镑:8:21⁄4. 未备资金的债务已申报为13 927 589英镑:2:2. 但战争引起的开支并没有随着和平的结束而结束;因此,虽然在1764年1月5日,资金筹供的债务(部分通过新贷款,部分通过资助无准备金债务)增加到129 586 789:10:13⁄4英镑,但仍有一笔资金筹供的债务(据英国贸易与金融考虑书的非常知情的作者说),这笔债务在当时和次年被记账,数额为9 975 017英镑:12:2 15/449英镑. 因此,据这位作者说,在1764年,由大不列颠共同出资和没有资金的公债达到139 561 807英镑:2:4.1757年作为新贷款的投保人保险费发放的终身年金,估计购买14年,价值为472 500英镑;1761年和1762年作为保险费发放的长期年金,估计购买27年半,价值为6 826 875英镑。 在大约七年的和平持续期间,阿姆斯特丹先生的谨慎和真正爱国的行政管理。佩勒姆无法偿还600万的旧债. 在一场几乎相同的持续战争中,新的债务已超过7 500万。

p45.original: On the 5th of January 1775, the funded debt of Great Britain amounted to £124,996,086, 1:6¼d. The unfunded, exclusive of a large civil-list debt, to £4,150,236:3:11 7/8. Both together, to £129,146,322:5:6. According to this account, the whole debt paid off, during eleven years of profound peace, amounted only to £10,415,476:16:9 7/8. Even this small reduction of debt, however, has not been all made from the savings out of the ordinary revenue of the state. Several extraneous sums, altogether independent of that ordinary revenue, have contributed towards it. Amongst these we may reckon an additional shilling in the pound land tax, for three years; the two millions received from the East-India company, as indemnification for their territorial acquisitions; and the one hundred and ten thousand pounds received from the bank for the renewal of their charter. To these must be added several other sums, which, as they arose out of the late war, ought perhaps to be considered as deductions from the expenses of it. The principal are,
p45.zh: 1775年1月5日,大不列颠的资金债务达到124,996,086英镑,即1:61⁄4d.资金无着落,不包括大量民价债务,为4,150,236英镑:3:11 7/8.两者合起来,为129,146,322:5:6. 根据这一说法,在11年的深刻和平期间,全部债务的偿付额仅为10,415,476英镑:16:9 7/8。 然而,即使如此微小的债务削减,也并非全部来自国家普通收入的节余。与普通收入完全无关的几笔不相干的款项也为它作出了贡献。 其中,我们可以考虑三年的英镑土地税增加一先令;从东印度公司收到的200万先令,作为对其领土收购的补偿;从银行收到的11万英磅,用于续订其章程。 此外,还必须加上其他一些款项,这些款项是战争后期产生的,也许应视为从战争费用中扣除。校长是,

p49.original: If we add to this sum the balance of the earl of Chatham's and Mr. Calcraft's accounts, and other army savings of the same kind, together with what has been received from the bank, the East-India company, and the additional shilling in the pound land tax, the whole must be a good deal more than five millions. The debt, therefore, which, since the peace, has been paid out of the savings from the ordinary revenue of the state, has not, one year with another, amounted to half a million a-year. The sinking fund has, no doubt, been considerably augmented since the peace, by the debt which had been paid off, by the reduction of the redeemable four per cents to three per cents, and by the annuities for lives which have fallen in; and, if peace were to continue, a million, perhaps, might now be annually spared out of it towards the discharge of the debt. Another million, accordingly, was paid in the course of last year; but at the same time, a large civil-list debt was left unpaid, and we are now involved in a new war, which, in its progress, may prove as expensive as any of our former wars. {It has proved more expensive than any one of our former wars, and has involved us in an additional debt of more than one hundred millions. During a profound peace of eleven years, little more than ten millions of debt was paid; during a war of seven years, more than one hundred millions was contracted.} The new debt which will probably be contracted before the end of the next campaign, may, perhaps, be nearly equal to all the old debt which has been paid off from the savings out of the ordinary revenue of the state. It would be altogether chimerical, therefore, to expect that the public debt should ever be completely discharged, by any savings which are likely to be made from that ordinary revenue as it stands at present.
p49.zh: 如果我们把查塔姆先生和查塔姆先生的耳朵的余下部分加到这个总数上Calcraft的帐户,以及其他同类的军队储蓄,加上从银行,东印度公司得到的,以及英镑土地税中增加的先令,整个必须是一个超过500万的好交易. 因此,自太平以来,这笔债务从国家普通收入的节余中支付,一年又一年没有达到每年50万美元。 毫无疑问,自和平以来,沉没基金已经大大增加,已经偿还的债务、可赎回的四分钱减少到3%以及生活年金已经减少;如果和平继续下去,现在每年也许有100万,也许可以免去100万,以清偿债务。 因此,去年又支付了一百万;但与此同时,大量民事债务没有得到偿还,我们现在正在卷入一场新的战争,战争在进行中可能证明与我们以前的任何战争一样昂贵。 {它证明比我们以前的任何战争都昂贵,而且涉及我们额外的一亿多债务。 在11年的深刻和平中,只偿还了1 000多万笔债务;在7年的战争中,约收了1亿多美元。 5 新的债务可能在下一次运动结束之前到期,也许几乎等于从国家普通收入中储蓄中还清的所有旧债务。 因此,期望公共债务永远能够完全通过目前这种普通收入可能带来的任何节余来得到清偿,是完全令人费解的。

p50.original: The public funds of the different indebted nations of Europe, particularly those of England, have, by one author, been represented as the accumulation of a great capital, superadded to the other capital of the country, by means of which its trade is extended, its manufactures are multiplied, and its lands cultivated and improved, much beyond what they could have been by means of that other capital only. He does not consider that the capital which the first creditors of the public advanced to government, was, from the moment in which he advanced it, a certain portion of the annual produce, turned away from serving in the function of a capital, to serve in that of a revenue; from maintaining productive labourers, to maintain unproductive ones, and to be spent and wasted, generally in the course of the year, without even the hope of any future reproduction. In return for the capital which they advanced, they obtained, indeed, an annuity of the public funds, in most cases, of more than equal value. This annuity, no doubt, replaced to them their capital, and enabled them to carry on their trade and business to the same, or, perhaps, to a greater extent than before; that is, they were enabled, either to borrow of other people a new capital, upon the credit of this annuity or, by selling it, to get from other people a new capital of their own, equal, or superior, to that which they had advanced to government. This new capital, however, which they in this manner either bought or borrowed of other people, must have existed in the country before, and must have been employed, as all capitals are, in maintaining productive labour. When it came into the hands of those who had advanced their money to government, though it was, in some respects, a new capital to them, it was not so to the country, but was only a capital withdrawn from certain employments, in order to be turned towards others. Though it replaced to them what they had advanced to government, it did not replace it to the country. Had they not advanced this capital to government, there would have been in the country two capitals, two portions of the annual produce, instead of one, employed in maintaining productive labour.
p50.zh: 欧洲不同债务国,特别是英格兰债务国的公共资金,据一位作者说,是该国另一资本的超级资本积累,通过这种资本扩大贸易、制造成倍增加、土地耕种和改善,远远超出了其他资本所能达到的程度。 他并不认为,公众最早的债权人向政府推进的资本,从他推进的那一刻起,就是年度生产的一部分,就不再从事资本的功能,而是从事收入的劳动;不再从事生产性劳动,而是从事非生产性劳动,而且被浪费和浪费,一般是在一年中,甚至没有未来再生产的任何希望. 为了换取他们所推进的资本,他们实际上获得了公共资金的年金,在大多数情况下,其价值超过等值。 毫无疑问,这种年金取代了他们的资本,使他们能够把贸易和业务维持到同样水平,或者甚至比以前更大幅度;也就是说,他们能够借他人新的资本,借取这种年金,或者通过出售这种资本,从其他人那里获得他们自己拥有的新资本,与他们向政府提出的新资本相等或优越。 然而,他们以这种方式购买或借用他人的这种新资本,必须在该国存在,而且必须像所有首都一样,受雇于维持生产性劳动。其时,虽于某些方面为官府提款者,虽为新资,而国非新资,而只为某某职所撤资之资,以转而为他人之资. 虽然它取代了他们向政府提出的计划,但它并没有取代国家。 如果它们不把这笔资本上缴给政府,该国本来会有两个首都,每年生产的两个部分,而不是一个,用于维持生产劳动。

p51.original: When, for defraying the expense of government, a revenue is raised within the year, from the produce of free or unmortgaged taxes, a certain portion of the revenue of private people is only turned away from maintaining one species of unproductive labour, towards maintaining another. Some part of what they pay in those taxes, might, no doubt, have been accumulated into capital, and consequently employed in maintaining productive labour; but the greater part would probably have been spent, and consequently employed in maintaining unproductive labour. The public expense, however, when defrayed in this manner, no doubt hinders, more or less, the further accumulation of new capital; but it does not necessarily occasion the destruction of any actually-existing capital.
p51.zh: 当为支付政府开支,一年之内从免征或未偿还税款中筹集到收入时,私人收入的某一部分只从维持一种非生产性劳动转为维持另一种非生产性劳动。无疑,他们在这些税中支付的部分可能已经积累成资本,并因此用于维持生产性劳动力;但大部分可能已经花费,因此用于维持非生产性劳动力。 然而,如果以这种方式支付公共开支,无疑会多少妨碍新资本的进一步积累;但它不一定造成任何实际存在的资本的破坏。

p52.original: When the public expense is defrayed by funding, it is defrayed by the annual destruction of some capital which had before existed in the country; by the perversion of some portion of the annual produce which had before been destined for the maintenance of productive labour, towards that of unproductive labour. As in this case, however, the taxes are lighter than they would have been, had a revenue sufficient for defraying the same expense been raised within the year; the private revenue of individuals is necessarily less burdened, and consequently their ability to save and accumulate some part of that revenue into capital, is a good deal less impaired. If the method of funding destroys more old capital, it, at the same time, hinders less the accumulation or acquisition of new capital, than that of defraying the public expense by a revenue raised within the year. Under the system of funding, the frugality and industry of private people can more easily repair the breaches which the waste and extravagance of government may occasionally make in the general capital of the society.
p52.zh: 如果公共开支由资金支付,则通过每年摧毁该国以前存在的一些资本来支付;将以前用于维持生产性劳动的部分年度产品转用于非生产性劳动。 然而,就本案而言,如果在一年内筹集到足以支付同样费用的收入,税收就比本来要轻;个人的私人收入必然负担较小,因此,他们能够将部分收入储蓄和积累成资本,这是一笔好生意,没有受到多大损害。 如果筹资方法破坏更多的旧资本,同时,它阻碍新资本的积累或收购的程度要小于通过一年内筹集的收入来支付公共开支。 在资金制度下,私人的节俭和工业可以更容易地修复政府偶尔在社会一般资本中造成的浪费和奢侈行为。

p53.original: It is only during the continuance of war, however, that the system of funding has this advantage over the other system. Were the expense of war to be defrayed always by a revenue raised within the year, the taxes from which that extraordinary revenue was drawn would last no longer than the war. The ability of private people to accumulate, though less during the war, would have been greater during the peace, than under the system of funding. War would not necessarily have occasioned the destruction of any old capitals, and peace would have occasioned the accumulation of many more new. Wars would, in general, be more speedily concluded, and less wantonly undertaken. The people feeling, during continuance of war, the complete burden of it, would soon grow weary of it; and government, in order to humour them, would not be under the necessity of carrying it on longer than it was necessary to do so. The foresight of the heavy and unavoidable burdens of war would hinder the people from wantonly calling for it when there was no real or solid interest to fight for. The seasons during which the ability of private people to accumulate was somewhat impaired, would occur more rarely, and be of shorter continuance. Those, on the contrary, during which that ability was in the highest vigour would be of much longer duration than they can well be under the system of funding.
p53.zh: 然而,只有在战争持续期间,筹资制度才具有比其他制度更有利的条件。 如果战争开支总是由一年之内筹集到的收入来支付,那么从中提取的特别收入的税收不会持续到战争。私人积累的能力,虽然在战争期间积累得更少,但在和平时期比在资助制度下积累得更大.战争不一定会摧毁任何旧首都,和平也会导致更多的新首都的积累。一般而言,战争将更快结束,而且不那么肆无忌惮。 在战争持续期间,人民感到其完全的负担很快会变得疲惫不堪;为了取笑他们,政府没有必要延长战争持续的时间。 对战争的沉重和不可避免的负担的预见,将阻碍人们在没有真正或坚实的利益来争取战争时,不无所求。私人积累能力受到一定损害的季节将很少出现,持续时间也较短。 相反,在这种能力发挥最大活力期间,其持续时间将比在供资制度下的时间长得多。

p54.original: When funding, besides, has made a certain progress, the multiplication of taxes which it brings along with it, sometimes impairs as much the ability of private people to accumulate, even in time of peace, as the other system would in time of war. The peace revenue of Great Britain amounts at present to more than ten millions a-year. If free and unmortgaged, it might be sufficient, with proper management, and without contracting a shilling of new debt, to carry on the most vigorous war. The private revenue of the inhabitants of Great Britain is at present as much incumbered in time of peace, their ability to accumulate is as much impaired, as it would have been in the time of the most expensive war, had the pernicious system of funding never been adopted.
p54.zh: 此外,当筹资取得一定进展时,它带来的税收的倍增有时会像其他制度在战争期间那样损害私人积累的能力,即使在和平时期也是如此。 大不列颠的和平收入目前每年超过1000万. 如果自由、不抵押,只要管理得当,而且不拖欠一先令的新债务,可能就足以进行最激烈的战争。 大不列颠居民的私人收入目前同和平时期一样多,他们的积累能力受到同样程度的损害,如果从未采用有害的筹资制度的话,这种能力在最昂贵的战争时期本来会受到同样的损害。

p55.original: In the payment of the interest of the public debt, it has been said, it is the right hand which pays the left. The money does not go out of the country. It is only a part of the revenue of one set of the inhabitants which is transferred to another; and the nation is not a farthing the poorer. This apology is founded altogether in the sophistry of the mercantile system; and, after the long examination which I have already bestowed upon that system, it may, perhaps, be unnecessary to say anything further about it. It supposes, besides, that the whole public debt is owing to the inhabitants of the country, which happens not to be true; the Dutch, as well as several other foreign nations, having a very considerable share in our public funds. But though the whole debt were owing to the inhabitants of the country, it would not, upon that account, be less pernicious.
p55.zh: 在支付公债利息时,据说是右手支付左手.钱不出国. 它只是一部分居民收入的一部分,转移给另一部分居民;国家不是穷人的远道而行。 这种道歉完全建立在商贸制度的理论中;而且,经过我已经给予该制度的长期审查,也许没有必要再进一步谈论这个问题。 此外,它还假设,全部公共债务是该国居民所欠的,这恰好不是事实;荷兰人以及其他几个外国在我国公共资金中占有相当大的份额。 但是,尽管全部债务是欠该国居民的,但从这一角度讲,这种债务不会更有害。

p56.original: Land and capital stock are the two original sources of all revenue, both private and public. Capital stock pays the wages of productive labour, whether employed in agriculture, manufactures, or commerce. The management of those two original sources of revenue belongs to two different sets of people; the proprietors of land, and the owners or employers of capital stock.
p56.zh: 土地和资本存量是所有收入的两个原始来源,无论是私人还是公共收入。资本存量支付生产性劳动力的工资,无论是从事农业、制造业还是商业。 这两个原始收入来源的管理属于两类不同的人:土地所有者以及资本存量的所有人或雇主。

p57.original: The proprietor of land is interested, for the sake of his own revenue, to keep his estate in as good condition as he can, by building and repairing his tenants houses, by making and maintaining the necessary drains and inclosures, and all those other expensive improvements which it properly belongs to the landlord to make and maintain. But, by different land taxes, the revenue of the landlord may be so much diminished, and, by different duties upon the necessaries and conveniencies of life, that diminished revenue may be rendered of so little real value, that he may find himself altogether unable to make or maintain those expensive improvements. When the landlord, however, ceases to do his part, it is altogether impossible that the tenant should continue to do his. As the distress of the landlord increases, the agriculture of the country must necessarily decline.
p57.zh: 土地的拥有者为了自己的收入而有兴趣通过建造和修理房客的房屋、制造和保持必要的排水沟和封闭设施以及所有它理应属于房东的所有其他昂贵的改良设施,尽可能地维持他的庄园。 但是,由于征收不同的土地税,地主的收入可能减少很多,由于对生活必需品和方便所负有的不同义务,收入减少可能使实际价值如此之小,以致他可能发现自己完全无法作出或维持这些昂贵的改善。 但是,当房东停止履行他的职责时,租户完全不可能继续履行他的职责。 随着地主的困扰增加,国家的农业必然会下降.

p58.original: When, by different taxes upon the necessaries and conveniencies of life, the owners and employers of capital stock find, that whatever revenue they derive from it, will not, in a particular country, purchase the same quantity of those necessaries and conveniencies which an equal revenue would in almost any other, they will be disposed to remove to some other. And when, in order to raise those taxes, all or the greater part of merchants and manufacturers, that is, all or the greater part of the employers of great capitals, come to be continually exposed to the mortifying and vexatious visits of the tax-gatherers, this disposition to remove will soon be changed into an actual removing. The industry of the country will necessarily fall with the removal of the capital which supported it, and the ruin of trade and manufactures will follow the declension of agriculture.
p58.zh: 当对生活必需品和方便地征收不同税时,资本库存的所有人和雇主发现,无论它们从中获取什么收入,在某一国家不会购买与几乎任何其他国家同等数量的必需品和方便地时,它们就会被转移到其他一些国家。 当为了提高这些税收,所有或更多的商家和制造商,即大首都的全体或大部分雇主,不断受到税收征收者令人痛心和烦恼的来访时,这种取消的倾向将很快转变为实际取消。国家的工业必然会随着支持它的首都的撤走而衰落,而贸易和制造的毁灭将随着农业的衰落而发生。

p59.original: To transfer from the owners of those two great sources of revenue, land, and capital stock, from the persons immediately interested in the good condition of every particular portion of land, and in the good management of every particular portion of capital stock, to another set of persons (the creditors of the public, who have no such particular interest ), the greater part of the revenue arising from either, must, in the long-run, occasion both the neglect of land, and the waste or removal of capital stock. A creditor of the public has, no doubt, a general interest in the prosperity of the agriculture, manufactures, and commerce of the country; and consequently in the good condition of its land, and in the good management of its capital stock. Should there be any general failure or declension in any of these things, the produce of the different taxes might no longer be sufficient to pay him the annuity or interest which is due to him. But a creditor of the public, considered merely as such, has no interest in the good condition of any particular portion of land, or in the good management of any particular portion of capital stock. As a creditor of the public, he has no knowledge of any such particular portion. He has no inspection of it. He can have no care about it. Its ruin may in some cases be unknown to him, and cannot directly affect him.
p59.zh: 从这两个大收入来源,即土地和资本存量的所有人,从对每一特定土地的良好状况和对每一特定部分资本存量的良好管理立即感兴趣的人,转移到另一组人(公共债权人,没有这种特殊利益),从长期来看,两者中产生的收入的较大部分必须同时引起对土地的忽视,以及资本存量的浪费或清除。 毫无疑问,公众的债权人对本国农业、制造业和商业的繁荣具有普遍利益;因此,对本国土地状况良好以及对资本库存的良好管理也具有普遍利益。 如果在其中任何一项中出现任何普遍失败或退税,不同税收的产值可能不再足以支付他应得的年金或利息。 但是,公众债权人,仅仅被视为公众债权人,对土地的任何特定部分的良好状况,或对资本的任何特定部分的良好管理,都没有任何利益。 作为公众的债权人,他不知道任何这种特定部分。 他没有检查过 他不会在乎的在某些情况下,他可能不知道会毁于一旦,不能直接影响到他。

p60.original: The practice of funding has gradually enfeebled every state which has adopted it. The Italian republics seem to have begun it. Genoa and Venice, the only two remaining which can pretend to an independent existence, have both been enfeebled by it. Spain seems to have learned the practice from the Italian republics, and (its taxes being probably less judicious than theirs) it has, in proportion to its natural strength, been-still more enfeebled. The debts of Spain are of very old standing. It was deeply in debt before the end of the sixteenth century, about a hundred years before England owed a shilling. France, notwithstanding all its natural resources, languishes under an oppressive load of the same kind. The republic of the United Provinces is as much enfeebled by its debts as either Genoa or Venice. Is it likely that, in Great Britain alone, a practice, which has brought either weakness or dissolution into every other country, should prove altogether innocent?
p60.zh: 资助的做法逐渐削弱了每一个采用这种做法的国家。 意大利共和国似乎已经开始了。热那亚和威尼斯, 剩下的唯一两个可以假装独立存在的, 都受到它的影响。 西班牙似乎从意大利共和国那里学到了这种做法,而且(其税收可能比其税收更不明智),根据其自然实力,西班牙仍然更加脆弱。 西班牙的债务已经很老套了。 在十六世纪末之前,它债务深重,比英格兰欠一先令还早了大约一百年. 尽管法国拥有所有自然资源,但它却在同样压迫性的负担下挣扎。联合各省共和国的债务与热那亚或威尼斯一样沉重。仅仅在大不列颠,一种已经给每一个其他国家带来软弱或解体的实践,是否应该证明是完全无辜的?

p61.original: The system of taxation established in those different countries, it may be said, is inferior to that of England. I believe it is so. But it ought to be remembered, that when the wisest government has exhausted all the proper subjects of taxation, it must, in cases of urgent necessity, have recourse to improper ones. The wise republic of Holland has, upon some occasions, been obliged to have recourse to taxes as inconvenient as the greater part of those of Spain. Another war, begun before any considerable liberation of the public revenue had been brought about, and growing in its progress as expensive as the last war, may, from irresistible necessity, render the British system of taxation as oppressive as that of Holland, or even as that of Spain. To the honour of our present system of taxation, indeed, it has hitherto given so little embarrassment to industry, that, during the course even of the most expensive wars, the frugality and good conduct of individuals seem to have been able, by saving and accumulation, to repair all the breaches which the waste and extravagance of government had made in the general capital of the society. At the conclusion of the late war, the most expensive that Great Britain ever waged, her agriculture was as flourishing, her manufacturers as numerous and as fully employed, and her commerce as extensive, as they had ever been before. The capital, therefore, which supported all those different branches of industry, must have been equal to what it had ever been before. Since the peace, agriculture has been still further improved; the rents of houses have risen in every town and village of the country, a proof of the increasing wealth and revenue of the people; and the annual amount of the greater part of the old taxes, of the principal branches of the excise and customs, in particular, has been continually increasing, an equally clear proof of an increasing consumption, and consequently of an increasing produce, which could alone support that consumption. Great Britain seems to support with ease, a burden which, half a century ago, nobody believed her capable of supporting, Let us not, however, upon this account, rashly conclude that she is capable of supporting any burden; nor even be too confident that she could support, without great distress, a burden a little greater than what has already been laid upon her.
p61.zh: 可以说,在这些国家建立的税收制度低于英格兰。 我相信是这样。 但应该记住,当最明智的政府用尽所有适当的税收对象时,它必须在紧急需要的情况下求助于不当的主体。 荷兰这个明智的共和国有时不得不像西班牙的大部分国家一样,不得不使用不方便的税收。另一场战争是在公共收入大量解放之前开始的,而且其进展与上一场战争一样昂贵,可能由于不可抗拒的需要,使英国的税收制度像荷兰的,甚至像西班牙的一样压迫。以我们目前的税收制度为荣,事实上,迄今为止,它并没有给工业带来什么尴尬,甚至在最昂贵的战争中,个人的节俭和良好行为似乎能够通过储蓄和积累来弥补政府浪费和奢侈在社会一般首都中犯下的所有违法行为。 在英国发动的最昂贵的战争末期,她的农业同样繁荣,她的制造商数量众多,就业也很多,她的商业也比以前更加广泛。 因此,支持所有这些不同行业的资本,必定与以前一样。 自和平以来,农业情况仍然得到进一步改善;全国每个城镇和村庄的住房租金都有所增加,这证明人民财富和收入都在增加;特别是消费和海关主要分支的旧税额每年增加,这同样清楚地证明,消费在增加,因此,产品在增加,而只有这些产品才能支持这种消费。 大不列颠似乎轻而易举地支持这一负担,半个世纪前,没有人相信她有能力支持这一负担。 然而,我们不要仓促地得出结论,她有能力承担任何负担;甚至不能过于自信地认为她能够不感到极大的痛苦地支持一个比已经赋予她的负担要大一点的负担。

p62.original: When national debts have once been accumulated to a certain degree, there is scarce, I believe, a single instance of their having been fairly and completely paid. The liberation of the public revenue, if it has ever been brought about at all, has always been brought about by a bankruptcy; sometimes by an avowed one, though frequently by a pretended payment.
p62.zh: 当国家债务一度积累到一定程度时,我认为,它们得到公平和完全偿付的单一例子是很少的。公共收入的解放,如果曾经带来过,总是由破产带来;有时是被宣告破产,尽管经常是被假装支付。

p63.original: The raising of the denomination of the coin has been the most usual expedient by which a real public bankruptcy has been disguised under the appearance of a pretended payment. If a sixpence, for example, should, either by act of parliament or royal proclamation, be raised to the denomination of a shilling, and twenty sixpences to that of a pound sterling; the person who, under the old denomination, had borrowed twenty shillings, or near four ounces of silver, would, under the new, pay with twenty sixpences, or with something less than two ounces. A national debt of about a hundred and twenty-eight millions, near the capital of the funded and unfunded debt of Great Britain, might, in this manner, be paid with about sixty-four millions of our present money. It would, indeed, be a pretended payment only, and the creditors of the public would really be defrauded of ten shillings in the pound of what was due to them. The calamity, too, would extend much further than to the creditors of the public, and those of every private person would suffer a proportionable loss; and this without any advantage, but in most cases with a great additional loss, to the creditors of the public. If the creditors of the public, indeed, were generally much in debt to other people, they might in some measure compensate their loss by paying their creditors in the same coin in which the public had paid them. But in most countries, the creditors of the public are, the greater part of them, wealthy people, who stand more in the relation of creditors than in that of debtors, towards the rest of their fellow citizens. A pretended payment of this kind, therefore, instead of alleviating, aggravates, in most cases, the loss of the creditors of the public; and, without any advantage to the public, extends the calamity to a great number of other innocent people. It occasions a general and most pernicious subversion of the fortunes of private people; enriching, in most cases, the idle and profuse debtor, at the expense of the industrious and frugal creditor; and transporting a great part of the national capital from the hands which were likely to increase and improve it, to those who are likely to dissipate and destroy it. When it becomes necessary for a state to declare itself bankrupt, in the same manner as when it becomes necessary for an individual to do so, a fair, open, and avowed bankruptcy, is always the measure which is both least dishonourable to the debtor, and least hurtful to the creditor. The honour of a state is surely very poorly provided for, when, in order to cover the disgrace of a real bankruptcy, it has recourse to a juggling trick of this kind, so easily seen through, and at the same time so extremely pernicious.
