p63.zh: 硬币面额的提高是实际公共破产在假付款的外表下变相的最为常见的权宜之计. 例如,如果六便士通过议会行为或皇家公告,升至先令的面额,26便士升至英镑的面额;在旧面额下借过二十先令,或接近四盎司银的人,在新面额下,将支付二十六便士,或不到两盎司的金额.大约1亿2千8百万的国债,接近大不列颠有资金和无资金的债务的资本,可能以这种方式用我们目前约6400万的现款来偿还。 这的确只是一种假装的付款,公众的债权人将真正被骗取10先令,即欠他们的英镑。这场灾难还将远远超出公共债权人的范围,每个私人的债权人将遭受可承受的损失;这对公共债权人没有任何好处,但在多数情况下还有很大的额外损失。 如果公共债权人通常对其他人欠债很多,他们可以在某种程度上通过用公共支付他们的硬币偿还债权人的债款来补偿他们的损失。 但是在大多数国家,公众的债权人,主要是富人,他们比债务人更关心其他同胞的债权人关系。 因此,在多数情况下,这种假付款不是减轻,而是加重了公众债权人的损失;在对公众没有任何好处的情况下,将灾难扩大到许多其他无辜人民。 它使私人财富受到普遍和最有害的颠覆;在大多数情况下,使闲置和挥霍的债务人富足,而牺牲勤劳和节俭的债权人;将国家资本的很大一部分从可能增加和改善的手中运送给那些可能分散和破坏资本的人。 当一国必须宣布自己破产时,以个人这样做所必要的同样方式,公平、公开和公开宣布破产,始终是债务人最不名誉和对债权人最不伤害的措施。一个国家的荣誉,当然没有为它提供多少,而为了掩盖真正的破产的耻辱,它却诉诸于这种杂耍的诡计,这种诡计很容易被看穿,同时又极其有害。

p64.original: Almost all states, however, ancient as well as modern, when reduced to this necessity, have, upon some occasions, played this very juggling trick. The Romans, at the end of the first Punic war, reduced the As, the coin or denomination by which they computed the value of all their other coins, from containing twelve ounces of copper, to contain only two ounces; that is, they raised two ounces of copper to a denomination which had always before expressed the value of twelve ounces. The republic was, in this manner, enabled to pay the great debts which it had contracted with the sixth part of what it really owed. So sudden and so great a bankruptcy, we should in the present times be apt to imagine, must have occasioned a very violent popular clamour. It does not appear to have occasioned any. The law which enacted it was, like all other laws relating to the coin, introduced and carried through the assembly of the people by a tribune, and was probably a very popular law. In Rome, as in all other ancient republics, the poor people were constantly in debt to the rich and the great, who, in order to secure their votes at the annual elections, used to lend them money at exorbitant interest, which, being never paid, soon accumulated into a sum too great either for the debtor to pay, or for any body else to pay for him. The debtor, for fear of a very severe execution, was obliged, without any further gratuity, to vote for the candidate whom the creditor recommended. In spite of all the laws against bribery and corruption, the bounty of the candidates, together with the occasional distributions of coin which were ordered by the senate, were the principal funds from which, during the latter times of the Roman republic, the poorer citizens derived their subsistence. To deliver themselves from this subjection to their creditors, the poorer citizens were continually calling out, either for an entire abolition of debts, or for what they called new tables; that is, for a law which should entitle them to a complete acquittance, upon paying only a certain proportion of their accumulated debts. The law which reduced the coin of all denominations to a sixth part of its former value, as it enabled them to pay their debts with a sixth part of what they really owed, was equivalent to the most advantageous new tables. In order to satisfy the people, the rich and the great were, upon several different occasions, obliged to consent to laws, both for abolishing debts, and for introducing new tables; and they probably were induced to consent to this law, partly for the same reason, and partly that, by liberating the public revenue, they might restore vigour to that government, of which they themselves had the principal direction. An operation of this kind would at once reduce a debt of £128,000,000 to £21,333,333:6:8. In the course of the second Punic war, the As was still further reduced, first, from two ounces of copper to one ounce, and afterwards from one ounce to half an ounce; that is, to the twenty-fourth part of its original value. By combining the three Roman operations into one, a debt of a hundred and twenty-eight millions of our present money, might in this manner be reduced all at once to a debt of £5,333,333:6:8. Even the enormous debt of Great Britain might in this manner soon be paid.
p64.zh: 然而,几乎所有的古老和现代的州,如果说成是这种必要的话,在某些情况下,都扮演了这种杂耍的伎俩。第一次普尼奇战争结束时,罗马人将As,即他们用来计算所有其他硬币价值的硬币或面额从12盎司的铜币减为仅含2盎司的铜币;也就是说,他们将2盎司的铜币升为以前一直表示12盎司价值的面额。共和国能够以这种方式偿还它所欠的六分之六的巨额债务。如此突然和如此伟大的破产,我们应当 在当今的时代 能够很好地想象, 一定引起了非常激烈的 流行的呼声。 它似乎没有产生任何结果。颁布该法的法律与所有其他有关硬币的法律一样,是由一个法官介绍和通过人民集会进行的,它可能是一部非常受欢迎的法律。在罗马,像其他所有古代共和国一样,穷人经常欠富人和大人们的债务,他们为了在年度选举中获得他们的选票,经常借高利贷给他们,而这种利息却从未支付过,很快积累成一个过高的金额,无论是债务人无力支付,还是任何其他机构无力支付。债务人担心会遭到非常严厉的处决,因此有义务在不给任何进一步好处的情况下,投票支持债权人推荐的候选人。 尽管有禁止贿赂和腐败的所有法律,候选人的恩惠以及参议院不时订购的硬币,是罗马共和国后期较贫穷的公民赖以维持生计的主要资金。 为了摆脱这种受制于债权人的状况,较贫穷的公民不断呼吁要么完全取消债务,要么要求他们所谓的新表格;也就是说,要求一项法律,规定他们只要支付其累积债务的一定比例,就有权完全免除债务。将所有面额的硬币减少到其原价值的第六部分的法律,因为它使得它们能够以它们实际所欠的第六部分来偿还债务,它相当于最有利的新表格。 为了满足人民、富人和大人们在几个不同场合都有义务同意法律,无论是为了取消债务还是为了提出新的表格;他们很可能被诱使同意该法律,部分原因是出于同样的原因,而且部分地是,通过释放公共收入,他们可以恢复政府活力,而政府本身是政府的主要方向。 这种业务将同时将128,000,000英镑的债务减少到21,333,333:6:8. 在第二次普尼奇战争中,阿斯号仍然进一步被削减,首先,从2盎司的铜牌减少到1盎司,随后从1盎司减少到了半盎司;即其原值的第24部分. 通过将罗马的三次行动合并为一,即一亿二千八百万我们现款的债务,可以这样一时全部减为5,333,333:6:8. 甚至大不列颠的巨额债务也可能很快以这种方式得到偿还.

p65.original: By means of such expedients, the coin of, I believe, all nations, has been gradually reduced more and more below its original value, and the same nominal sum has been gradually brought to contain a smaller and a smaller quantity of silver.
p65.zh: 我相信,通过这种权宜之计,所有国家的硬币已逐渐减少,越来越低于其原始价值,同样的名义金额也逐渐地被带入银币中,其数量越来越少。

p66.original: Nations have sometimes, for the same purpose, adulterated the standard of their coin; that is, have mixed a greater quantity of alloy in it. If in the pound weight of our silver coin, for example, instead of eighteen penny-weight, according to the present standard, there were mixed eight ounces of alloy; a pound sterling, or twenty shillings of such coin, would be worth little more than six shillings and eightpence of our present money. The quantity of silver contained in six shillings and eightpence of our present money, would thus be raised very nearly to the denomination of a pound sterling. The adulteration of the standard has exactly the same effect with what the French call an augmentation, or a direct raising of the denomination of the coin.
p66.zh: 各国有时为了同一目的,伪造其硬币的标准;也就是说,将更多的合金混合在硬币中。 如果用我们的银币的磅重,而不是按目前的标准,18美分的重量,则有8盎司合金的混合;一英镑,或20先令的这种硬币,价值将小于我们目前钱的6先令和8便士. 因此,我们现款的六先令和八便士中所含的白银数量将几乎提高到英镑的面值。标准的掺假与法国人所称的增币,或直接提高硬币面额的效果完全相同.

p67.original: An augmentation, or a direct raising of the denomination of the coin, always is, and from its nature must be, an open and avowed operation. By means of it, pieces of a smaller weight and bulk are called by the same name, which had before been given to pieces of a greater weight and bulk. The adulteration of the standard, on the contrary, has generally been a concealed operation. By means of it, pieces are issued from the mint, of the same denomination, and, as nearly as could be contrived, of the same weight, bulk, and appearance, with pieces which had been current before of much greater value. When king John of France, {See Du Cange Glossary, voce Moneta; the Benedictine Edition.} in order to pay his debts, adulterated his coin, all the officers of his mint were sworn to secrecy. Both operations are unjust. But a simple augmentation is an injustice of open violence; whereas an adulteration is an injustice of treacherous fraud. This latter operation, therefore, as soon as it has been discovered, and it could never be concealed very long, has always excited much greater indignation than the former. The coin, after any considerable augmentation, has very seldom been brought back to its former weight; but after the greatest adulterations, it has almost always been brought back to its former fineness. It has scarce ever happened, that the fury and indignation of the people could otherwise be appeased.
p67.zh: 硬币面额的扩大或直接提高,从性质上来说,始终是公开和公开的操作。 通过它,重量较小的块块和块状的块块被叫作同名的,这以前是交给重量较大的块块和块状的. 相反,该标准的掺假一般是一种隐蔽的行动。 通过这种方式,从同一种面额的薄荷中发行了同样重量、批量和外观的碎片,这些碎片以前的价值要高得多。 当法国国王约翰,{见杜坎格词汇,voce Moneta;The Benedictine Edition.}为了还债,他伪造了他的硬币,他薄荷的所有官员都宣誓保密.这两项行动都是不公正的。 但是,简单的增加是公开暴力的不公正;而通奸是欺骗的不公正。 因此,一旦发现后一项行动,而且永远无法隐瞒,就一直比前一项行动激起更大的愤慨。硬币经过任何大幅度的增量后,很少恢复到以前的重量;但是经过最大规模的掺假后,几乎总是恢复到以前的精美.鲜有发生,否则人民愤怒和愤慨就会得到平息。

p68.original: In the end of the reign of Henry VIII., and in the beginning of that of Edward VI., the English coin was not only raised in its denomination, but adulterated in its standard. The like frauds were practised in Scotland during the minority of James VI. They have occasionally been practised in most other countries.
p68.zh: 在亨利八世统治的末期,以及爱德华六世统治的开始,英国硬币不仅在面额上被提升,而且以标准成假币. 在苏格兰,在詹姆斯六世的少数时期也存在类似的欺诈行为。 大多数其他国家也偶尔实行这种制度。

p69.original: That the public revenue of Great Britain can never be completely liberated, or even that any considerable progress can ever be made towards that liberation, while the surplus of that revenue, or what is over and above defraying the annual expense of the peace establishment, is so very small, it seems altogether in vain to expect. That liberation, it is evident, can never be brought about, without either some very considerable augmentation of the public revenue, or some equally considerable reduction of the public expense.
p69.zh: 大不列颠的公共收入永远不能完全解放,甚至不可能在实现这一解放方面取得任何重大进展,而这种收入的盈余,或超出支付和平建设年度开支的部分,却如此之少,似乎完全没有结果。 显然,如果不大幅度地增加公共收入,或同样大幅度地减少公共开支,这种解放是永远不可能实现的。

p70.original: A more equal land tax, a more equal tax upon the rent of houses, and such alterations in the present system of customs and excise as those which have been mentioned in the foregoing chapter, might, perhaps, without increasing the burden of the greater part of the people, but only distributing the weight of it more equally upon the whole, produce a considerable augmentation of revenue. The most sanguine projector, however, could scarce flatter himself, that any augmentation of this kind would be such as could give any reasonable hopes, either of liberating the public revenue altogether, or even of making such progress towards that liberation in time of peace, as either to prevent or to compensate the further accumulation of the public debt in the next war.
p70.zh: 土地税更加平等,对房屋租金征收更加平等的税,以及上文提到的对目前海关和消费制度的这种改变,也许不会增加大部分人民的负担,但只会使整个土地的重量更加平均地分配,从而大大增加收入。 然而,最乐观的投影员却很少自夸,任何这种增加都将给人任何合理的希望,要么是完全释放公共收入,要么是在和平时期朝着这一解放迈进,要么是防止或补偿下一次战争中公共债务的进一步积累。

p71.original: By extending the British system of taxation to all the different provinces of the empire, inhabited by people either of British or European extraction, a much greater augmentation of revenue might be expected. This, however, could scarce, perhaps, be done, consistently with the principles of the British constitution, without admitting into the British parliament, or, if you will, into the states-general of the British empire, a fair and equal representation of all those different provinces; that of each province bearing the same proportion to the produce of its taxes, as the representation of Great Britain might bear to the produce of the taxes levied upon Great Britain. The private interest of many powerful individuals, the confirmed prejudices of great bodies of people, seem, indeed, at present, to oppose to so great a change, such obstacles as it may be very difficult, perhaps altogether impossible, to surmount. Without, however, pretending to determine whether such a union be practicable or impracticable, it may not, perhaps, be improper, in a speculative work of this kind, to consider how far the British system of taxation might be applicable to all the different provinces of the empire; what revenue might be expected from it, if so applied; and in what manner a general union of this kind might be likely to affect the happiness and prosperity of the differrent provinces comprehended within it. Such a speculation, can, at worst, be regarded but as a new Utopia, less amusing, certainly, but no more useless and chimerical than the old one.
p71.zh: 通过将英国的税收制度扩大到帝国的所有不同省份,包括英国人或欧洲人,可以预期收入会大大增加。 然而,也许这很少能做到,符合英国宪法的原则,不向英国议会承认,或者,如果你愿意的话,向大英帝国的各国总司令承认,所有这些不同省份都有公平、平等的代表性;每个省份的税收比例与大不列颠的税收比例相同,而大不列颠的代表权可能对对大不列颠征收的税收的产量负责。 许多有权势的个人的私人利益,以及经证实的伟大人民身体的偏见,似乎确实在目前反对如此巨大的改变,这些障碍可能很难克服,也许完全不可能克服。 然而,如果不假装确定这种结合是实际的还是不实际的,那么在这种投机性的工作中,考虑英国的税收制度在多大程度上可以适用于帝国的所有不同省份,如果适用这种制度,可以指望从中获得什么收入,以及这种总的结合会以何种方式影响不同省份的幸福和繁荣,也许并不是不适当的。 这种猜测,最糟糕的是,可以被看作是一个新的乌托邦, 不那么有趣,当然,但没有什么比旧的更无用和浪漫。

p72.original: The land-tax, the stamp duties, and the different duties of customs and excise, constitute the four principal branches of the British taxes.
p72.zh: 地税,印花税,以及海关和消费税的不同关税构成英国税的四大分支.

p73.original: Ireland is certainly as able, and our American and West India plantations more able, to pay a land tax, than Great Britain. Where the landlord is subject neither to tythe nor poor's rate, he must certainly be more able to pay such a tax, than where he is subject to both those other burdens. The tythe, where there is no modus, and where it is levied in kind, diminishes more what would otherwise be the rent of the landlord, than a land tax which really amounted to five shillings in the pound. Such a tythe will be found, in most cases, to amount to more than a fourth part of the real rent of the land, or of what remains after replacing completely the capital of the farmer, together with his reasonable profit. If all moduses and all impropriations were taken away, the complete church tythe of Great Britain and Ireland could not well be estimated at less than six or seven millions. If there was no tythe either in Great Britain or Ireland, the landlords could afford to pay six or seven millions additional land tax, without being more burdened than a very great part of them are at present. America pays no tythe, and could, therefore, very well afford to pay a land tax. The lands in America and the West Indies, indeed, are, in general, not tenanted nor leased out to farmers. They could not, therefore, be assessed according to any rent roll. But neither were the lands of Great Britain, in the 4th of William and Mary, assessed according to any rent roll, but according to a very loose and inaccurate estimation. The lands in America might be assessed either in the same manner, or according to an equitable valuation, in consequence of an accurate survey, like that which was lately made in the Milanese, and in the dominions of Austria, Prussia, and Sardinia.
p73.zh: 爱尔兰当然比大不列颠更有能力支付土地税,我们的美国和西印度种植园也更有能力。 如果房东不受制于泰特人或穷人的税率,他肯定比他承受其他两种负担更有能力支付这种税。泰特人,在没有临时工的地方,在实物征收的地方,比实际相当于英镑5先令的土地税,更能减少地主的租金。在大多数情况下,这种土司将相当于土地实际租金的四分之一以上,或者完全取代农民资本后剩下的部分,加上他的合理利润。 如果所有的作案手法和所有不适当的行为都被拿走,那么大不列颠和爱尔兰的完整的教堂建筑估计不可能少于六七百万. 如果在大不列颠或爱尔兰没有土地税,地主可以负担六、七百万额外的土地税,而不必承受比目前大部分土地更沉重的负担。 美国不付任何税费,因此,美国完全有能力支付土地税。 事实上,美国和西印度群岛的土地一般不出租,也不出租给农民。 因此,无法按照任何租金表来评估这些款项。 但大不列颠的土地,在威廉和玛丽的第四世中,也没有按照任何租借卷来评估,而是根据非常松散和不准确的估计来评估. 美国的土地可能以同样的方式评估,或者根据公平估价, 以准确调查的结果, 就像最近在米兰, 以及奥地利,普鲁士,和撒丁岛的统治。

p74.original: Stamp duties, it is evident, might be levied without any variation, in all countries where the forms of law process, and the deeds by which property, both real and personal, is transferred, are the same, or nearly the same.
p74.zh: 显而易见,在法律程序形式以及转让财产的实际和个人行为相同或几乎相同的国家,可以不加任何改变地征收印花税。

p75.original: The extension of the custom-house laws of Great Britain to Ireland and the plantations, provided it was accompanied, as in justice it ought to be, with an extension of the freedom of trade, would be in the highest degree advantageous to both. All the invidious restraints which at present oppress the trade of Ireland, the distinction between the enumerated and non-enumerated commodities of America, would be entirely at an end. The countries north of Cape Finisterre would be as open to every part of the produce of America, as those south of that cape are to some parts of that produce at present. The trade between all the different parts of the British empire would, in consequence of this uniformity in the custom-house laws, be as free as the coasting trade of Great Britain is at present. The British empire would thus afford, within itself, an immense internal market for every part of the produce of all its different provinces. So great an extension of market would soon compensate, both to Ireland and the plantations, all that they could suffer from the increase of the duties of customs.
p75.zh: 将大不列颠的海关法扩大到爱尔兰和种植园,只要这样做与司法一样,同时扩大贸易自由,对两者都最有利。 目前压迫爱尔兰贸易的所有令人反感的限制,以及美国所列举的商品和未加工商品之间的区别,都将完全结束。菲尼斯特尔角以北的国家对美国每一部分产品都开放,而披风以南的国家对目前某些部分产品开放。 大英帝国所有不同部分之间的贸易,由于海关法的这种统一性,将像大不列颠目前沿海贸易一样自由。 因此,大英帝国本身将为其所有不同省份的每一部分产品提供巨大的内部市场。如此巨大的市场扩张将很快补偿爱尔兰和种植园,它们可能因关税增加而蒙受的一切损失。

p76.original: The excise is the only part of the British system of taxation, which would require to be varied in any respect, according as it was applied to the different provinces of the empire. It might be applied to Ireland without any variation; the produce and consumption of that kingdom being exactly of the same nature with those of Great Britain. In its application to America and the West Indies, of which the produce and consumption are so very different from those of Great Britain, some modification might be necessary, in the same manner as in its application to the cyder and beer counties of England.
p76.zh: 消费税是英国税收制度的唯一部分,它要求在任何方面有所改变,因为它适用于帝国的不同省份. 它可以不加任何改变地适用于爱尔兰;该王国的生产和消费与大不列颠的生产和消费性质完全相同。 在适用于美国和西印度群岛,其中的生产和消费与大不列颠大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸大陸

p77.original: A fermented liquor, for example, which is called beer, but which, as it is made of molasses, bears very little resemblance to our beer, makes a considerable part of the common drink of the people in America. This liquor, as it can be kept only for a few days, cannot, like our beer, be prepared and stored up for sale in great breweries; but every private family must brew it for their own use, in the same manner as they cook their victuals. But to subject every private family to the odious visits and examination of the tax-gatherers, in the same manner as we subject the keepers of ale-houses and the brewers for public sale, would be altogether inconsistent with liberty. If, for the sake of equality, it was thought necessary to lay a tax upon this liquor, it might be taxed by taxing the material of which it is made, either at the place of manufacture, or, if the circumstances of the trade rendered such an excise improper, by laying a duty upon its importation into the colony in which it was to be consumed. Besides the duty of one penny a-gallon imposed by the British parliament upon the importation of molasses into America, there is a provincial tax of this kind upon their importation into Massachusetts Bay, in ships belonging to any other colony, of eight-pence the hogshead; and another upon their importation from the northern colonies into South Carolina, of five-pence the gallon. Or, if neither of these methods was found convenient, each family might compound for its consumption of this liquor, either according to the number of persons of which it consisted, in the same manner as private families compound for the malt tax in England; or according to the different ages and sexes of those persons, in the same manner as several different taxes are levied in Holland; or, nearly as Sir Matthew Decker proposes, that all taxes upon consumable commodities should be levied in England. This mode of taxation, it has already been observed, when applied to objects of a speedy consumption, is not a very convenient one. It might be adopted, however, in cases where no better could be done.
p77.zh: 例如一种发酵的酒,它叫做啤酒, 但是,由于它是由糖浆制成的, 和我们的啤酒没有什么相似之处, 使美国人民喝的酒占了相当大一部分。 这种酒,由于只能保存几天,不能像我们的啤酒一样,准备和储存起来,在大酿酒厂销售;但是,每个私人家庭必须自己酿造,用在自己烹饪的口味上. 但是,让每个私人家庭接受令人憎恶的探访和税收征收者的检查,就像我们把独家住宅的保管人和酿酒商作为公共销售对象那样,这完全不符合自由。 如果为平等起见,认为有必要对酒类征税,则可以在制造地对酒类的原料征税,或者在贸易情况使这种消费不适当时,在将酒类进口到消费的殖民地时规定一项义务。 除了英国议会对向美国进口糖浆规定一分钱一加仑的义务外,在从马萨诸塞湾进口时,在属于任何其他殖民地的船舶上,对猪头八便士征收这种税;在从北部殖民地进口到南卡罗莱纳州时,对猪头五便士征收这种税。 或者,如果发现这两种方法都不方便,那么每个家庭都可能会因饮用这种酒而复合,或者根据其组成人数,以与在英国征收麦芽税的私人家庭复合的方式;或者根据这些人的不同年龄和性别,以与在荷兰征收的几种不同税相同的方式;或者,几乎正如马修·德克尔爵士建议的那样,所有消费商品的税收都应在英国征收。 这种征税方式在适用于迅速消费的对象时,已经很不方便。 但是,如果无法做得更好,则可以采用这一办法。

p78.original: Sugar, rum, and tobacco, are commodities which are nowhere necessaries of life, which are become objects of almost universal consumption, and which are, therefore, extremely proper subjects of taxation. If a union with the colonies were to take place, those commodities might be taxed, either before they go out of the hands of the manufacturer or grower; or, if this mode of taxation did not suit the circumstances of those persons, they might be deposited in public warehouses, both at the place of manufacture, and at all the different ports of the empire, to which they might afterwards be transported, to remain there, under the joint custody of the owner and the revenue officer, till such time as they should be delivered out, either to the consumer, to the merchant-retailer for home consumption, or to the merchant-exporter; the tax not to be advanced till such delivery. When delivered out for exportation, to go duty-free, upon proper security being given, that they should really be exported out of the empire. These are, perhaps, the principal commodities, with regard to which the union with the colonies might require some considerable change in the present system of British taxation.
p78.zh: 糖、朗姆酒和烟草是生活必需品,几乎成为普遍消费的对象,因此是极为适当的税收主体。 如果与殖民地建立联盟,这些商品可以在从制造商或种植者手中运出之前征税;或者,如果这种征税方式不符合这些人的情况,则可以将其存放在公共仓库,无论是在制造地点,还是在帝国所有不同的港口,然后可能将其运往这些港口,由货主和税务官共同保管,直至交付给消费者、商贩家用或商贩;在交货前不得预支税款。 当运出出口时,在得到适当的安全后,可以免税,即它们应该真正从帝国出口。 这些或许是主要商品,与殖民地的联盟可能需要对英国目前的税收制度作一些相当大的改变。

p79.original: What might be the amount of the revenue which this system of taxation, extended to all the different provinces of the empire, might produce, it must, no doubt, be altogether impossible to ascertain with tolerable exactness. By means of this system, there is annually levied in Great Britain, upon less than eight millions of people, more than ten millions of revenue. Ireland contains more than two millions of people, and, according to the accounts laid before the congress, the twelve associated provinces of America contain more than three. Those accounts, however, may have been exaggerated, in order, perhaps, either to encourage their own people, or to intimidate those of this country; and we shall suppose, therefore, that our North American and West Indian colonies, taken together, contain no more than three millions; or that the whole British empire, in Europe and America, contains no more than thirteen millions of inhabitants. If, upon less than eight millions of inhabitants, this system of taxation raises a revenue of more than ten millions sterling; it ought, upon thirteen millions of inhabitants, to raise a revenue of more than sixteen millions two hundred and fifty thousand pounds sterling. From this revenue, supposing that this system could produce it, must be deducted the revenue usually raised in Ireland and the plantations, for defraying the expense of the respective civil governments. The expense of the civil and military establishment of Ireland, together with the interest of the public debt, amounts, at a medium of the two years which ended March 1775, to something less than seven hundred and fifty thousand pounds a year. By a very exact account of the revenue of the principal colonies of America and the West Indies, it amounted, before the commencement of the present disturbances, to a hundred and forty-one thousand eight hundred pounds. In this account, however, the revenue of Maryland, of North Carolina, and of all our late acquisitions, both upon the continent, and in the islands, is omitted; which may, perhaps, make a difference of thirty or forty thousand pounds. For the sake of even numbers, therefore, let us suppose that the revenue necessary for supporting the civil government of Ireland and the plantations may amount to a million. There would remain, consequently, a revenue of fifteen millions two hundred and fifty thousand pounds, to be applied towards defraying the general expense of the empire, and towards paying the public debt. But if, from the present revenue of Great Britain, a million could, in peaceable times, be spared towards the payment of that debt, six millions two hundred and fifty thousand pounds could very well be spared from this improved revenue. This great sinking fund, too, might be augmented every year by the interest of the debt which had been discharged the year before; and might, in this manner, increase so very rapidly, as to be sufficient in a few years to discharge the whole debt, and thus to restore completely the at-present debilitated and languishing vigour of the empire. In the meantime, the people might be relieved from some of the most burdensome taxes; from those which are imposed either upon the necessaries of life, or upon the materials of manufacture. The labouring poor would thus be enabled to live better, to work cheaper, and to send their goods cheaper to market. The cheapness of their goods would increase the demand for them, and consequently for the labour of those who produced them. This increase in the demand for labour would both increase the numbers, and improve the circumstances of the labouring poor. Their consumption would increase, and, together with it, the revenue arising from all those articles of their consumption upon which the taxes might be allowed to remain.
p79.zh: 帝国所有不同省份的税收制度可能产生多少收入? 毫无疑问,这种税收制度完全无法以可容忍的准确性加以确定。 通过这一制度,英国每年征收不到800万人的收入,超过1 000万的收入。 爱尔兰有200多万人,根据大会前的叙述,美国12个相关省份有3个以上。 但是,这些说法可能被夸大,或许是为了鼓励本国人民,或恐吓这个国家的人民;因此,我们假定,我们北美和西印度殖民地合计不超过300万;或者整个大英帝国在欧美的居住人数不超过1 300万。 如果对不到800万居民来说,这种税收制度能增加1 000万英镑的收入;对1 300万居民来说,应该增加1 600多万25万英镑的收入。假定这种制度能够产生这种收入,就必须从这种收入中扣除爱尔兰和种植园通常筹集的收入,以支付各地方政府的费用。 爱尔兰民事和军事机构的费用,加上公共债务利息,在1775年3月结束的两年的中期内,每年达75万英镑以下。 根据对美国和西印度群岛主要殖民地收入的非常精确的叙述,在目前的动乱开始之前,该收入达到141,000,800英镑。 然而,在这个账户中,马里兰州,北卡罗莱纳州的收入,以及我们后来在大陆和岛屿上获得的所有收入,都省略了;这也许可以产生三、四万英镑的差别。 因此,为了平均数字起见,让我们假设,支持爱尔兰民政政府和种植园所需的收入可能达到一百万。 因此,仍有15亿25万英镑的收入,将用于支付帝国的一般开支和偿还公共债务。 但是,如果从大不列颠目前的收入来看,在和平时期,100万英镑能够免于偿还这一债务,那么600万25万英镑就完全可以从这种改善的收入中幸免。这笔巨大的沉没基金每年也可能因前一年偿还的债务利息而增加;而且可能以这种方式迅速增加,在几年内足以清偿全部债务,从而完全恢复帝国目前衰弱和疲惫的活力。 与此同时,人民可以免除一些负担最重的税收;可以免除那些对生活必需品或制造材料施加的税收。 这样,劳动穷人就能过上更好的生活,更便宜地工作,并将他们的商品更便宜地送到市场。其商品的廉价性将增加对商品的需求,从而增加生产商品的人的劳动力需求。劳动力需求的增长既会增加劳动力数量,也会改善正在从事劳动的穷人的处境。 他们的消费将增加,再加上这些消费物品所产生的收入,这些物品的税收可能仍可保留。

p80.original: The revenue arising from this system of taxation, however, might not immediately increase in proportion to the number of people who were subjected to it. Great indulgence would for some time be due to those provinces of the empire which were thus subjected to burdens to which they had not before been accustomed; and even when the same taxes came to be levied everywhere as exactly as possible, they would not everywhere produce a revenue proportioned to the numbers of the people. In a poor country, the consumption of the principal commodities subject to the duties of customs and excise, is very small; and in a thinly inhabited country, the opportunities of smuggling are very great. The consumption of malt liquors among the inferior ranks of people in Scotland is very small; and the excise upon malt, beer, and ale, produces less there than in England, in proportion to the numbers of the people and the rate of the duties, which upon malt is different, on account of a supposed difference of quality. In these particular branches of the excise, there is not, I apprehend, much more smuggling in the one country than in the other. The duties upon the distillery, and the greater part of the duties of customs, in proportion to the numbers of people in the respective countries, produce less in Scotland than in England, not only on account of the smaller consumption of the taxed commodities, but of the much greater facility of smuggling. In Ireland, the inferior ranks of people are still poorer than in Scotland, and many parts of the country are almost as thinly inhabited. In Ireland, therefore, the consumption of the taxed commodities might, in proportion to the number of the people, be still less than in Scotland, and the facility of smuggling nearly the same. In America and the West Indies, the white people, even of the lowest rank, are in much better circumstances than those of the same rank in England; and their consumption of all the luxuries in which they usually indulge themselves, is probably much greater. The blacks, indeed, who make the greater part of the inhabitants, both of the southern colonies upon the continent and of the West India islands, as they are in a state of slavery, are, no doubt, in a worse condition than the poorest people either in Scotland or Ireland. We must not, however, upon that account, imagine that they are worse fed, or that their consumption of articles which might be subjected to moderate duties, is less than that even of the lower ranks of people in England. In order that they may work well, it is the interest of their master that they should be fed well, and kept in good heart, in the same manner as it is his interest that his working cattle should be so. The blacks, accordingly, have almost everywhere their allowance of rum, and of molasses or spruce-beer, in the same manner as the white servants; and this allowance would not probably be withdrawn, though those articles should be subjected to moderate duties. The consumption of the taxed commodities, therefore, in proportion to the number of inhabitants, would probably be as great in America and the West Indies as in any part of the British empire. The opportunities of smuggling, indeed, would be much greater; America, in proportion to the extent of the country, being much more thinly inhabited than either Scotland or Ireland. If the revenue, however, which is at present raised by the different duties upon malt and malt liquors, were to be levied by a single duty upon malt, the opportunity of smuggling in the most important branch of the excise would be almost entirely taken away; and if the duties of customs, instead of being imposed upon almost all the different articles of importation, were confined to a few of the most general use and consumption, and if the levying of those duties were subjected to the excise laws, the opportunity of smuggling, though not so entirely taken away, would be very much diminished. In consequence of those two apparently very simple and easy alterations, the duties of customs and excise might probably produce a revenue as great, in proportion to the consumption of the most thinly inhabited province, as they do at present, in proportion to that of the most populous.
p80.zh: 然而,这种税收制度所产生的收入可能不会立即按照受此制度约束的人数的比例增加。 在一段时间内,帝国的省份将受到极大的宽容,因此它们承受着以前未曾习惯的负担;即使尽可能准确地在任何地方征收同样的税费,它们也不会在任何地方产生与人口数量成比例的收入。在一个贫穷国家,关税和消费税的主要商品的消费非常少;在一个人口稀少的国家,走私的机会非常大。苏格兰低级人群中麦芽酒的消费量非常小;麦芽酒,啤酒和啤酒的消费量与英格兰相比,按人口数量和关税率的比例生产量较少,而麦芽酒则因质量的假定差异而有所不同. 在这些特别的消费分支中,我发现,在一个国家,走私活动比在另一个国家多得多。蒸馏厂的关税,以及海关的更大部分关税,按各自国家的人数比例,苏格兰的产量比英格兰少,这不仅是因为所税商品的消费较少,而且走私设施也大得多。 在爱尔兰,低等阶层的人仍然比苏格兰更穷,全国很多地区几乎都一样人口稀疏. 因此,在爱尔兰,按人口数量的比例,被征税商品的消费可能仍然低于苏格兰,而走私设施几乎相同。在美国和西印度群岛,白人,即使是地位最低的白人,在环境上也比英国的同级人好得多;他们消费所有他们通常放纵的奢侈品,可能要大得多. 事实上,那些使大部分居民,无论是非洲大陆上的南方殖民地还是西印度群岛的居民,都处于奴役状态的黑人,无疑比苏格兰或爱尔兰的最贫穷者处于更糟糕的状况。 然而,我们决不能因此想象他们吃得更苦,或者他们消费可能要承担轻度义务的物品,甚至比英格兰较低阶层的人还少。其为善用,宜其主人,以善养之,以善养之,与他之业牛,亦同其利益. 因此,黑人几乎在任何地方都有与白人仆人一样的朗姆酒和糖浆或酿酒的补贴;这种补贴可能不会撤销,尽管这些条款应当服从于适度的职责。 因此,按居民人数的比例,在美国和西印度群岛的消费可能与大英帝国的任何地方一样大。 事实上,走私的机会将大得多;按国家范围的比例,美国比苏格兰或爱尔兰人口少得多。 但是,如果目前由麦芽酒和麦芽酒不同关税筹集的收入要由麦芽酒单一税征收,则消费品中最重要的分支的走私机会几乎将完全丧失;如果海关的关税不是强加于几乎所有不同的进口品,而是限于少数最普遍的用途和消费,如果征收这些税需遵守消费法,那么走私的机会虽然没有完全丧失,但将会大大减少。 由于这两个显然非常简单和容易的改变,关税和消费税可能会产生与目前人口最稀少省份的消费成比例的巨额收入,与人口最多省份的消费成比例。

p81.original: The Americans, it has been said, indeed, have no gold or silver money, the interior commerce of the country being carried on by a paper currency; and the gold and silver, which occasionally come among them, being all sent to Great Britain, in return for the commodities which they receive from us. But without gold and silver, it is added, there is no possibility of paying taxes. We already get all the gold and silver which they have. How is it possible to draw from them what they have not?
p81.zh: 据说,美国人确实没有金银两钱,国内的商贸用纸币进行;而金银,偶尔也到他们中间,都送到大不列颠,以换取他们从我们那里得到的商品. 但无金银,则加之,则无纳税之可能. 我们已经拿到他们所有的金银了如何从他们那里汲取他们所没有的东西?

p82.original: The present scarcity of gold and silver money in America, is not the effect of the poverty of that country, or of the inability of the people there to purchase those metals. In a country where the wages of labour are so much higher, and the price of provisions so much lower than in England, the greater part of the people must surely have wherewithal to purchase a greater quantity, if it were either necessary or convenient for them to do so. The scarcity of those metals, therefore, must be the effect of choice, and not of necessity.
p82.zh: 目前美国金银钱的稀缺性不是该国贫困的影响,也不是那里的人民无力购买这些金属的影响.在一个劳动工资如此高,供给价格如此低于英国的国家,如果必要或方便,则大部分人民肯定有购买更多数量的财力。 因此,这些金属的稀缺必须是选择的结果,而不是必要性。

p83.original: It is for transacting either domestic or foreign business, that gold or silver money is either necessary or convenient.
p83.zh: 黄金或银钱是必要或方便的,用于交易国内或国外业务。

p84.original: The domestic business of every country, it has been shewn in the second book of this Inquiry, may, at least in peaceable times, be transacted by means of a paper currency, with nearly the same degree of conveniency as by gold and silver money. It is convenient for the Americans, who could always employ with profit, in the improvement of their lands, a greater stock than they can easily get, to save as much as possible the expense of so costly an instrument of commerce as gold and silver; and rather to employ that part of their surplus produce which would be necessary for purchasing those metals, in purchasing the instruments of trade, the materials of clothing, several parts of household furniture, and the iron work necessary for building and extending their settlements and plantations; in purchasing not dead stock, but active and productive stock. The colony governments find it for their interest to supply the people with such a quantity of paper money as is fully sufficient, and generally more than sufficient, for transacting their domestic business. Some of those governments, that of Pennsylvania, particularly, derive a revenue from lending this paper money to their subjects, at an interest of so much per cent. Others, like that of Massachusetts Bay, advance, upon extraordinary emergencies, a paper money of this kind for defraying the public expense; and afterwards, when it suits the conveniency of the colony, redeem it at the depreciated value to which it gradually falls. In 1747, {See Hutchinson's History of Massachusetts Bay vol. ii. page 436 et seq.} that colony paid in this manner the greater part of its public debts, with the tenth part of the money for which its bills had been granted. It suits the conveniency of the planters, to save the expense of employing gold and silver money in their domestic transactions; and it suits the conveniency of the colony governments, to supply them with a medium, which, though attended with some very considerable disadvantages, enables them to save that expense. The redundancy of paper money necessarily banishes gold and silver from the domestic transactions of the colonies, for the same reason that it has banished those metals from the greater part of the domestic transactions in Scotland; and in both countries, it is not the poverty, but the enterprizing and projecting spirit of the people, their desire of employing all the stock which they can get, as active and productive stock, which has occasioned this redundancy of paper money.
p84.zh: 每个国家的国内事务,在本调查的第二本书中都曾提到过,至少在平和的时期,可能通过纸币进行交易,与金银钱几乎具有同等程度的通融.美国人总是能够以利润来改善自己的土地,比他们容易得到的多,他们可以尽量省去昂贵的黄金和白银等商业工具的费用;而可以使用购买这些金属所必需的剩余产品,购买贸易工具、服装材料、家庭家具的几部分,以及建造和扩大定居点和种植园所需的铁料;购买的不是死粮,而是活粮和生产性库存。殖民地政府出于自身利益,认为应向人民提供足够多的纸币,以便他们能够进行国内交易。其中一些政府,特别是宾夕法尼亚州政府,从向国民借出这笔纸币中获得收入,利息高达百分之五十。其他人,如马萨诸塞湾,在非常紧急情况下,预支一笔这类纸币,以支付公共开支;随后,当它适合殖民地的容留时,按它逐渐跌落的折余价值赎回。1747年,{见哈钦森的马萨诸塞湾历史vol. ii. pap 436 et except.}该殖民地以这种方式偿还了大部分公共债务,其中第10部分是其账单获得的。 它适合种植园主的宽容,以节省在国内交易中使用金银货币的费用;它适合殖民地政府的宽容,以提供一种媒介,虽然这种媒介存在一些非常严重的不利之处,但使他们能够节省这笔费用。纸币的冗余必然将黄金和白银从殖民地的国内交易中放逐,其原因同样在于它将这些金属从苏格兰国内交易的大部分中放逐出来;在两个国家,这不是贫穷,而是人民兴旺和表现的精神,他们希望把能够获得的所有库存作为活跃和生产性的库存来使用,这导致了纸币的冗余。

p85.original: In the exterior commerce which the different colonies carry on with Great Britain, gold and silver are more or less employed, exactly in proportion as they are more or less necessary. Where those metals are not necessary, they seldom appear. Where they are necessary, they are generally found.
p85.zh: 在不同的殖民地与大不列颠进行的外商交易中,金银或多或少被雇佣,其比例恰好是多少是必需的. 在不需要这些金属的地方,它们很少出现。必要时,一般会找到它们。

p86.original: In the commerce between Great Britain and the tobacco colonies, the British goods are generally advanced to the colonists at a pretty long credit, and are afterwards paid for in tobacco, rated at a certain price. It is more convenient for the colonists to pay in tobacco than in gold and silver. It would be more convenient for any merchant to pay for the goods which his correspondents had sold to him, in some other sort of goods which he might happen to deal in, than in money. Such a merchant would have no occasion to keep any part of his stock by him unemployed, and in ready money, for answering occasional demands. He could have, at all times, a larger quantity of goods in his shop or warehouse, and he could deal to a greater extent. But it seldom happens to be convenient for all the correspondents of a merchant to receive payment for the goods which they sell to him, in goods of some other kind which he happens to deal in. The British merchants who trade to Virginia and Maryland, happen to be a particular set of correspondents, to whom it is more convenient to receive payment for the goods which they sell to those colonies in tobacco, than in gold and silver. They expect to make a profit by the sale of the tobacco; they could make none by that of the gold and silver. Gold and silver, therefore, very seldom appear in the commerce between Great Britain and the tobacco colonies. Maryland and Virginia have as little occasion for those metals in their foreign, as in their domestic commerce. They are said, accordingly, to have less gold and silver money than any other colonies in America. They are reckoned, however, as thriving, and consequently as rich, as any of their neighbours.
p86.zh: 在大不列颠和烟草殖民地之间的商业中,英国商品一般以相当长的功劳向殖民者高级,之后以烟草支付,以一定的价格评分.殖民者比用金银来支付烟草更方便。任何商人支付其通讯员卖给他的货物比支付金钱更方便,在某种他可能碰巧交易的其他货物中。这样的商人没有机会让他的股票中的任何一部分失业,并且随时用钱来应付不时的要求。 他可以随时在他的商店或仓库中拥有更多的货物,他可以进行更大的交易。 但是,一个商人的所有通讯员很少能以他碰巧交易的某种其他种类的货物得到他们卖给他的货物的付款。向弗吉尼亚州和马里兰州交易的英国商人恰好是一组特定的通讯员,比起黄金和白银,他们向这些殖民地出售的烟草商品更方便地收到付款. 他们期望通过销售烟草来赚钱;他们无法通过黄金和白银来赚钱。 因此,黄金和白银很少出现在大不列颠和烟草殖民地之间的商业中。马里兰州和弗吉尼亚州的外国金属 和国内商业一样少见。 因此,据说他们拥有的金银钱比美国任何其他殖民地都少。 然而,人们却认为,他们与任何邻国一样,繁荣昌盛,因而富有。

p87.original: In the northern colonies, Pennsylvania, New York, New Jersey, the four governments of New England, etc. the value of their own produce which they export to Great Britain is not equal to that of the manufactures which they import for their own use, and for that of some of the other colonies, to which they are the carriers. A balance, therefore, must be paid to the mother-country in gold and silver and this balance they generally find.
p87.zh: 在北部殖民地,宾夕法尼亚州,纽约州,新泽西州,新英格兰四国政府等,它们出口到大不列颠的自产农产品的价值,不等于它们进口用于自己用途的制成品的价值,而对于其他一些殖民地来说,它们也是这些殖民地的载体. 因此,必须用金银向母国支付余额,而且这些余额一般都存在。

p88.original: In the sugar colonies, the value of the produce annually exported to Great Britain is much greater than that of all the goods imported from thence. If the sugar and rum annually sent to the mother-country were paid for in those colonies, Great Britain would be obliged to send out, every year, a very large balance in money; and the trade to the West Indies would, by a certain species of politicians, be considered as extremely disadvantageous. But it so happens, that many of the principal proprietors of the sugar plantations reside in Great Britain. Their rents are remitted to them in sugar and rum, the produce of their estates. The sugar and rum which the West India merchants purchase in those colonies upon their own account, are not equal in value to the goods which they annually sell there. A balance, therefore, must necessarily be paid to them in gold and silver, and this balance, too, is generally found.
p88.zh: 在糖类聚居区,每年出口到大不列颠的农产品价值远大于从这里进口的所有商品. 如果每年寄给祖国的糖和朗姆酒在这些殖民地得到支付,大不列颠将不得不每年送出一笔非常大的资金余额;而向西印度群岛的贸易,被某些政治人物视为极其不利。 但是,糖厂的许多主要业主都居住在英国,这恰巧是这样的。 他们的租金以糖和朗姆酒汇给他们,这是他们庄园的产物. 西印度商人自己在这些殖民地购买的糖和朗姆酒,与其每年出售的商品价值不相等。 因此,必须用金银来支付余额,而且这种余额也普遍存在。

p89.original: The difficulty and irregularity of payment from the different colonies to Great Britain, have not been at all in proportion to the greatness or smallness of the balances which were respectively due from them. Payments have, in general, been more regular from the northern than from the tobacco colonies, though the former have generally paid a pretty large balance in money, while the latter have either paid no balance, or a much smaller one. The difficulty of getting payment from our different sugar colonies has been greater or less in proportion, not so much to the extent of the balances respectively due from them, as to the quantity of uncultivated land which they contained; that is, to the greater or smaller temptation which the planters have been under of over-trading, or of undertaking the settlement and plantation of greater quantities of waste land than suited the extent of their capitals. The returns from the great island of Jamaica, where there is still much uncultivated land, have, upon this account, been, in general, more irregular and uncertain than those from the smaller islands of Barbadoes, Antigua, and St. Christopher's, which have, for these many years, been completely cultivated, and have, upon that account, afforded less field for the speculations of the planter. The new acquisitions of Grenada, Tobago, St. Vincent's, and Dominica, have opened a new field for speculations of this kind; and the returns front those islands have of late been as irregular and uncertain as those from the great island of Jamaica.
p89.zh: 不同殖民地向大不列颠支付款项的困难和不规则,与它们各自应付的余额的大小完全不相称。总的来说,北方的付款比烟草殖民地的付款更经常,尽管前者一般支付相当大一笔资金,而后者要么没有支付任何余额,要么支付数额要小得多。 从我们不同的糖类聚居区获得付款的困难程度很大,与它们分别应得的余额程度不相称,与它们所包含未开垦土地的数量不相称;也就是说,由于种植者受到的过度交易的多少诱惑,或者由于承担了比其首都范围更大规模的荒地的安置和种植园。 牙买加大岛仍有许多未开垦的土地,因此,与较小的巴巴多斯岛、安提瓜岛和圣塔岛相比,从牙买加返回的人总的来说更加不规则和不确定。克里斯托弗的,这些年来, 已经完全种植了, 并且,根据这个理由, 给予较少的田地 来进行种植者的猜测。格林纳达、多巴哥、圣多巴哥的新收购文森特岛和多米尼克岛为这种投机开辟了新的领域;这些岛屿的回归战线最近与来自牙买加大岛的岛屿一样不规则和不确定。

p90.original: It is not, therefore, the poverty of the colonies which occasions, in the greater part of them, the present scarcity of gold and silver money. Their great demand for active and productive stock makes it convenient for them to have as little dead stock as possible, and disposes them, upon that account, to content themselves with a cheaper, though less commodious instrument of commerce, than gold and silver. They are thereby enabled to convert the value of that gold and silver into the instruments of trade, into the materials of clothing, into household furniture, and into the iron work necessary for building and extending their settlements and plantations. In those branches of business which cannot be transacted without gold and silver money, it appears, that they can always find the necessary quantity of those metals; and if they frequently do not find it, their failure is generally the effect, not of their necessary poverty, but of their unnecessary and excessive enterprise. It is not because they are poor that their payments are irregular and uncertain, but because they are too eager to become excessively rich. Though all that part of the produce of the colony taxes, which was over and above what was necessary for defraying the expense of their own civil and military establishments, were to be remitted to Great Britain in gold and silver, the colonies have abundantly wherewithal to purchase the requisite quantity of those metals. They would in this case be obliged, indeed, to exchange a part of their surplus produce, with which they now purchase active and productive stock, for dead stock. In transacting their domestic business, they would be obliged to employ a costly, instead of a cheap instrument of commerce; and the expense of purchasing this costly instrument might damp somewhat the vivacity and ardour of their excessive enterprise in the improvement of land. It might not, however, be necessary to remit any part of the American revenue in gold and silver. It might be remitted in bills drawn upon, and accepted by, particular merchants or companies in Great Britain, to whom a part of the surplus produce of America had been consigned, who would pay into the treasury the American revenue in money, after having themselves received the value of it in goods; and the whole business might frequently be transacted without exporting a single ounce of gold or silver from America.
p90.zh: 因此,不是殖民地的贫困,在大部分殖民地中,金银钱目前短缺。 他们对活跃和生产性库存的巨大需求,使得他们能够尽可能少地拥有枯萎的库存,并以此为计,以比黄金和白银更便宜、但又不那么商品化的商业工具来处置这些库存。 因此,他们能够将这种金银的价值转化为贸易工具、服装材料、家用家具以及建造和扩大定居点和种植园所需的铁制工作。 在那些没有金银钱无法交易的工商部门中,看来它们总是能够找到这些金属的必要数量;如果它们经常找不到这些金属,它们的失败通常是其后果,而不是其必要的贫穷,而是其不必要的和过度的事业。 他们的付款不定期、不确定,不是因为他们贫穷,而是因为他们太急于过度富裕。 虽然殖民地的税收中除了支付其民用和军事机构的费用之外,其余所有部分都要用黄金和白银汇给大不列颠,但殖民地拥有购买这些金属的必要数量的充分资源。 在这种情况下,它们确实有义务将一部分剩余产品交换给现在它们购买的活跃和生产性库存,以换取枯萎的库存。 在进行国内交易时,它们必须使用昂贵的而不是廉价的商业工具;购买这种昂贵的工具的费用可能在一定程度上潮湿了它们在改善土地方面的过度企业的活力和热情。 然而,也许没有必要汇出美国黄金和白银收入的任何部分。它可以汇入从大不列颠抽取的账单,并被大不列颠的特定商人或公司接受,美国的部分剩余产品已经汇给这些商人或公司,他们将在自己收到美国在货物中的收入后,将这笔收入汇入国库;整个企业可能经常进行交易,而不从美国出口一盎司黄金或银子。

p91.original: It is not contrary to justice, that both Ireland and America should contribute towards the discharge of the public debt of Great Britain. That debt has been contracted in support of the government established by the Revolution; a government to which the protestants of Ireland owe, not only the whole authority which they at present enjoy in their own country, but every security which they possess for their liberty, their property, and their religion; a government to which several of the colonies of America owe their present charters, and consequently their present constitution; and to which all the colonies of America owe the liberty, security, and property, which they have ever since enjoyed. That public debt has been contracted in the defence, not of Great Britain alone, but of all the different provinces of the empire. The immense debt contracted in the late war in particular, and a great part of that contracted in the war before, were both properly contracted in defence of America.
p91.zh: 爱尔兰和美国都应该为偿还大不列颠的公共债务作出贡献,这不违反正义。这笔债务是用来支持革命所建立的政府的;爱尔兰抗议者不仅对爱尔兰政府负有全部责任,他们现在在其本国享有的全部权力,而且对其自由、财产和宗教所拥有的一切安全,一个美国几个殖民地必须履行现行宪章,因此也是其现行宪法,所有美国殖民地都享有从此享有的自由、安全和财产。公债是国防所包办的,不光是大不列颠,而是帝国所有不同省份的公债.特别是战争后期的巨额债务,以及战争前的很大一部分债务,都是为保卫美国而适当收缩的。

p92.original: By a union with Great Britain, Ireland would gain, besides the freedom of trade, other advantages much more important, and which would much more than compensate any increase of taxes that might accompany that union. By the union with England, the middling and inferior ranks of people in Scotland gained a complete deliverance from the power of an aristocracy, which had always before oppressed them. By a union with Great Britain, the greater part of people of all ranks in Ireland would gain an equally complete deliverance from a much more oppressive aristocracy; an aristocracy not founded, like that of Scotland, in the natural and respectable distinctions of birth and fortune, but in the most odious of all distinctions, those of religious and political prejudices; distinctions which, more than any other, animate both the insolence of the oppressors, and the hatred and indignation of the oppressed, and which commonly render the inhabitants of the same country more hostile to one another than those of different countries ever are. Without a union with Great Britain, the inhabitants of Ireland are not likely, for many ages, to consider themselves as one people.
p92.zh: 如果与大不列颠结盟,爱尔兰除了贸易自由之外,还将获得其他更重要的好处,这些好处将远远不止于补偿该联盟可能增加的任何税收。通过与英格兰的联盟,苏格兰的居高临下的人阶层从一个以前一直压迫他们的贵族政权中获得了完全的救赎。通过与大不列颠的联盟,爱尔兰各阶层的大多数人将同样从更压迫性的贵族统治中获得完全的救赎;一个贵族统治不是像苏格兰那样在天生和财富的天生和可敬的区别上建立的,而是在所有区别上最令人憎恶的,宗教和政治偏见的区别;这种区别比任何其他区别更能刺激压迫者的傲慢,以及被压迫者的仇恨和愤慨,而且通常使同一国家的居民彼此比不同国家的居民更加敌对。 没有与大不列颠的联盟,爱尔兰的居民在许多年中不可能把自己视为一个民族.

p93.original: No oppressive aristocracy has ever prevailed in the colonies. Even they, however, would, in point of happiness and tranquillity, gain considerably by a union with Great Britain. It would, at least, deliver them from those rancourous and virulent factions which are inseparable from small democracies, and which have so frequently divided the affections of their people, and disturbed the tranquillity of their governments, in their form so nearly democratical. In the case of a total separation from Great Britain, which, unless prevented by a union of this kind, seems very likely to take place, those factions would be ten times more virulent than ever. Before the commencement of the present disturbances, the coercive power of the mother-country had always been able to restrain those factions from breaking out into any thing worse than gross brutality and insult. If that coercive power were entirely taken away, they would probably soon break out into open violence and bloodshed. In all great countries which are united under one uniform government, the spirit of party commonly prevails less in the remote provinces than in the centre of the empire. The distance of those provinces from the capital, from the principal seat of the great scramble of faction and ambition, makes them enter less into the views of any of the contending parties, and renders them more indifferent and impartial spectators of the conduct of all. The spirit of party prevails less in Scotland than in England. In the case of a union, it would probably prevail less in Ireland than in Scotland; and the colonies would probably soon enjoy a degree of concord and unanimity, at present unknown in any part of the British empire. Both Ireland and the colonies, indeed, would be subjected to heavier taxes than any which they at present pay. In consequence, however, of a diligent and faithful application of the public revenue towards the discharge of the national debt, the greater part of those taxes might not be of long continuance, and the public revenue of Great Britain might soon be reduced to what was necessary for maintaining a moderate peace-establishment.
p93.zh: 在殖民地中从未有过压迫性的贵族统治。 然而,即使他们,从幸福和安宁的角度来看,也会因与大不列颠的结合而大有收获。 它至少能将他们从那些与小民主国家密不可分的愤怒和恶毒的派别中解救出来,这些派别经常分裂人民的感情,以如此接近民主的形式扰乱其政府的安宁。 如果完全脱离大不列颠,除非受到这种联盟的阻挠,否则,这些派别似乎极有可能发生,其威力将比任何时候都高十倍。 在目前的动乱开始之前,祖国的胁迫力量一直能够阻止这些派别爆发出比粗暴的暴行和侮辱更糟糕的举动。 如果这种胁迫性力量被完全夺走,他们很可能很快会爆发为公开的暴力和流血。在所有统一政府下统一起来的伟大国家中,在边远省份中,党的精神通常比在帝国中部更为盛行。 这些省份远离首都,远离各派别和雄心壮志的主要位置,使它们较少地进入任何争斗党派的观点,使他们更加漠不关心和不偏不倚地观察所有党派的行为。 在苏格兰,党的精神比在英格兰要少。 就联合而言,爱尔兰的联盟可能比苏格兰的联盟要少;殖民地很可能很快享有一定程度的和谐和一致,目前大英帝国的任何地方都不得而知。 事实上,爱尔兰和殖民地都将受到比它们目前支付的任何税额都重的税收。 然而,由于对偿还国家债务认真和忠实地运用公共收入,这些税收的大部分可能不会长久持续下去,而且大不列颠的公共收入可能很快减少到维持温和的和平建设所必需的水平。

p94.original: The territorial acquisitions of the East India Company, the undoubted right of the Crown, that is, of the state and people of Great Britain, might be rendered another source of revenue, more abundant, perhaps, than all those already mentioned. Those countries are represented as more fertile, more extensive, and, in proportion to their extent, much richer and more populous than Great Britain. In order to draw a great revenue from them, it would not probably be necessary to introduce any new system of taxation into countries which are already sufficiently, and more than sufficiently, taxed. It might, perhaps, be more proper to lighten than to aggravate the burden of those unfortunate countries, and to endeavour to draw a revenue from them, not by imposing new taxes, but by preventing the embezzlement and misapplication of the greater part of those which they already pay.
p94.zh: 东印度公司的领土收购,即英国王室,即大不列颠的州和人民毫无疑问的权利,可能会成为另一个收入来源,也许比上述所有来源更为丰富。这些国家的代表比大不列颠更加肥沃、更加广泛,而且按其规模的比例,更富有、人口更多。 为了从中获取大量收入,可能没有必要在已经征税足够和足够多的国家中引入任何新的税收制度。 或许,减轻而不是加重这些不幸国家的负担,并努力从它们那里获得收入,这也许更合适,不是通过征收新的税,而是通过防止它们已经支付的大部分资金被挪用和滥用。

p95.original: If it should be found impracticable for Great Britain to draw any considerable augmentation of revenue from any of the resources above mentioned, the only resource which can remain to her, is a diminution of her expense. In the mode of collecting and in that of expending the public revenue, though in both there may be still room for improvement, Great Britain seems to be at least as economical as any of her neighbours. The military establishment which she maintains for her own defence in time of peace, is more moderate than that of any European state, which can pretend to rival her either in wealth or in power. None of these articles, therefore, seem to admit of any considerable reduction of expense. The expense of the peace-establishment of the colonies was, before the commencement of the present disturbances, very considerable, and is an expense which may, and, if no revenue can be drawn from them, ought certainly to be saved altogether. This constant expense in time of peace, though very great, is insignificant in comparison with what the defence of the colonies has cost us in time of war. The last war, which was undertaken altogether on account of the colonies, cost Great Britain, it has already been observed, upwards of ninety millions. The Spanish war of 1739 was principally undertaken on their account; in which, and in the French war that was the consequence of it, Great Britain, spent upwards of forty millions; a great part of which ought justly to be charged to the colonies. In those two wars, the colonies cost Great Britain much more than double the sum which the national debt amounted to before the commencement of the first of them. Had it not been for those wars, that debt might, and probably would by this time, have been completely paid; and had it not been for the colonies, the former of those wars might not, and the latter certainly would not, have been undertaken. It was because the colonies were supposed to be provinces of the British Empire, that this expense was laid out upon them. But countries which contribute neither revenue nor military force towards the support of the empire, cannot be considered as provinces. They may, perhaps, be considered as appendages, as a sort of splendid and shewy equipage of the empire. But if the empire can no longer support the expense of keeping up this equipage, it ought certainly to lay it down; and if it cannot raise its revenue in proportion to its expense, it ought at least to accommodate its expense to its revenue. If the colonies, notwithstanding their refusal to submit to British taxes, are still to be considered as provinces of the British empire, their defence, in some future war, may cost Great Britain as great an expense as it ever has done in any former war. The rulers of Great Britain have, for more than a century past, amused the people with the imagination that they possessed a great empire on the west side of the Atlantic. This empire, however, has hitherto existed in imagination only. It has hitherto been, not an empire, but the project of an empire; not a gold mine, but the project of a gold mine; a project which has cost, which continues to cost, and which, if pursued in the same way as it has been hitherto, is likely to cost, immense expense, without being likely to bring any profit; for the effects of the monopoly of the colony trade, it has been shewn, are to the great body of the people, mere loss instead of profit. It is surely now time that our rulers should either realize this golden dream, in which they have been indulging themselves, perhaps, as well as the people; or that they should awake from it themselves, and endeavour to awaken the people. If the project cannot be completed, it ought to be given up. If any of the provinces of the British empire cannot be made to contribute towards the support of the whole empire, it is surely time that Great Britain should free herself from the expense of defending those provinces in time of war, and of supporting any part of their civil or military establishment in time of peace; and endeavour to accommodate her future views and designs to the real mediocrity of her circumstances.
p95.zh: 如果认为英国无法从上述任何资源中提取任何可观的增加收入,那么她唯一能够保留的资源就是削减她的开支。 在征收和支出公共收入的方式中,虽然两者都可能仍有改进的余地,但大不列颠似乎至少与任何邻国一样经济。 在和平时期,她为保卫自己而维持的军事体制比任何欧洲国家都温和,因为欧洲国家可以假装在财富或权力上与她竞争。 因此,这些条款似乎都未承认可大幅度削减开支。 在目前的动乱开始之前,建立殖民地的费用是相当可观的,如果无法从中获取收入,这笔费用当然应该全部节省。 这种和平时期的不断开支,虽然非常巨大,但与殖民地的防卫在战时给我们造成的损失相比,是微不足道的.上次战争是完全由于殖民地而发动的,它使英国付出了代价,已经观察到了9 000万以上。1739年的西班牙战争主要是由他们负责进行的;在战争中,以及由此引起的法国战争中,大不列颠花费了4000万以上;其中很大一部分应该被正当地征收给殖民地. 在这两场战争中,殖民地使大不列颠付出了比第一次战争开始前国债多一倍多的代价。 如果不是这些战争,债务可能,而且可能届时已经完全偿还;如果不是殖民地,这些战争的前一种可能,而后一种可能,当然不会,已经完全偿还。 正是因为殖民地本来是大英帝国的省份,所以这笔费用被花在了他们身上. 但是,既不提供收入,也不提供军事力量支持帝国的国家,不能被视为省份. 也许,它们可以被视为附属物, 是帝国的一种精美而精致的装备。 但是如果帝国再不能支持维持这种装备的费用,它当然应该放下它;如果帝国不能按照它的开支比例增加它的收入,它至少应该将它的开支计入它的收入. 如果殖民地尽管拒绝向英国缴税,但仍被视作大英帝国的省份,那么在将来的某次战争中,他们的防卫可能会像以前任何战争中那样花费大不列颠的巨额费用. 大不列颠的统治者们在一个多世纪前,以想象中他们拥有大西洋西侧的伟大帝国而使人民感到欢欣鼓舞. 然而,这个帝国至今仅存在于想象中. 它至今不是帝国,而是帝国的工程;不是金矿,而是金矿的工程;一个已经耗资,仍在继续耗资的项目,如果沿用至今的同样方式进行,很可能耗资巨大,不会带来任何利润;由于殖民地贸易的垄断影响,它一直被抛在人民身上,只是损失而不是利润. 我们的统治者现在肯定应该认识到这个金色的梦想,也许他们一直在这个梦中,以及人民自己和人民都沉浸其中;或者他们应该从它中醒来,努力唤醒人民。 如果项目无法完成,应当放弃. 如果大英帝国的任何省份不能为整个帝国的支持作出贡献,那肯定是时候大不列颠应该摆脱战争时期保卫这些省份的费用,以及和平时期支持其民用或军事机构的任何部分的费用;并努力将她的未来观点和计划与她的实际平庸情况相适应。
